review: i have been to this location during covid-19 and have not had any problems being seen for treatment of my migraine. i only come in when it's at it's worse and i need a shot to keep it from going on for days. i recently had one in late april here with no problem. due to a migraine i have been in bed all day and not been able to eat or drink so i finally went before 5pm to be seen. i was turned away by the charge nurse jahnna  eastman. she wanted me to go to another location where they send people with covid-19 symptoms. my temperature was never taken and she said that headaches were on the list of symptoms. i suffer from migraines which i am on preventive medication for. when my medication doesn't work i go in to receive alternative care. jahnna stated that some people were more lenient and she wanted to see my kaiser number to check and see who allowed me to be seen. this is a hospital. you are their staff. you should all have the same standards. she turned me away finally saying that she had another patient. it was completely empty at this time. as we drove off we saw no line of people just the staff talking. i understand you are doing your job but having compassion should also be part of your interaction. i went home to now wait out my migraine because despite being healthy i was told i wasn't allowed to be seen here. maybe you are a compassionate nurse but not to me and not on this day. to be clear i think this location is good but i wanted to share my experience because things could always be better.

i recently gave birth to my first baby at the abrazo location, and i just have to say i was very impressed with the staff and service i received while there, despite the rumors i've heard about labor and delivery. i gave birth during the coronavirus pandemic and the nurses were professional and made sure my husband and i were taken care of. i want to give a shout out specifically to a traveling nurse lindsey who helped me so much through delivery and made sure i was comfortable the whole time. i also want to give a shout out to another nurse denise who helped my husband and i during the recovery period and was so personable and professional. despite the circumstance, my husband and i were overall pleased with our stay. especially because of the service we received from lindsey and denise. the food however i will give 2 stars. that's my only complaint.

had surgery a month ago. it was scheduled prior to the pandemic and was worried it would have to be postponed. was able to have the surgery as planned.  very grateful to the staff that cared for me prior to and post operation. they were attentive to my needs and answered my questions regarding my recovery. even received a letter a week later signed by all the staff.  sincere thank you to all the dedicated professionals that are working to take care of everyone during this stressful time in our history.

0 score for this e.r spent les than 5 min checking me told me i had corona virus and to go home to quarantine also the er ppl took no precaution acted like it was nothing at all no big deal you'll have a fever you be fine . even after i gave a huge week history of temps over 102 . biggest mistake ever to go here .. go to t bird banner they are on top of it 100%

i visited the er for chest pain tonight. i drove myself as i didn't want to waste time waiting for an ambulance. once inside, their focus was on the fake flu, not a possible heart attack! then i was told to "have a seat". note that i didn't see any other patients... just employees, casually talking amongst themselves.
after about 20 minutes i returned to the window and requested they give me my id back because i was leaving! they refused! then someone finally came out and took me into the screening room. again, i asked for my id... "nope". about ten minutes later they did an ekg.
about 30 minutes later another nurse came in to take me to x-ray. i asked her for my id and she said "we will be back in about two minutes, i'll get it for you then." which she did. by then i was feeling much better (on my own) so i continued to wait.
then i sat for another 10-15 minutes in the waiting room inside.
a nurse came up and wanted to start an iv, by this time i was feeling much better and thought i could make it to a better hospital. i asked to talk to a doctor first... because i was considering walking out. 
she took me to a room in the er, where i waited alone for almost 2 hours! i never saw a doctor!
during my long wait, i was able to observe about 6-10 staff members in the nurses station. none doing much other than chatting amongst themselves and snacking. they were wearing masks... but not on their faces!
since i was alone, and personally believe this current flu ordeal is 100% political, i too removed my mask.
shorty after someone came in to update my payment info. as they entered i put my mask on. for their comfort, not mine!
shortly after a very rude woman, staff member, came in and ordered that i was to wear a mask the entire time i was there!
i told her that if it's really that important, she should tell the 6-10 employees to put theirs on! she ignored me!
after finishing up with my personal info, i asked who that rude woman was... apparently just a secretary of some sort!
i told them i was leaving, & walked out! 
on my way to another hospital, i instructed my son to hire a lawyer if i had medical issues on my way to a safer hospital. he promised he would.
fortunately for the rude secretary, the incompetent staff and the hospital, nothing bad happened. i won't be returning!
if they are foolish enough to send me a bill... we will be going to court!

i don't like leaving a bad review during a time like this, when things are frustrating and stressful for all of us, let alone hospital staff at the front lines of a pandemic. but whatever your personal feelings about a patient are, nurses in the er at the nurses' station shouldn't make fun of and mock their patients for ten minutes where they can hear every single word while receiving no care whatsoever. one nurse, the one making most of the comments, put the tv remote on my lap (no tv in the room that i saw) instead of the call button as well when i was not yet in a position to find it myself. regardless of whether you believe i am experiencing an emergency (it obviously feels like one to me or i would never be in the er), to make fun of a condition i was born with and am waiting to hear if i need neurosurgery for is also disheartening. this was a crushing experience for me. thank you to the nurse who actually looked after me today, who is extremely nice and compassionate and wished me well with my neurosurgery appointment. i hope all of you stay healthy and safe, but that some learn kindness from others and that words matter.

gallstones! uff...yep that's what brought me here! painful like crazy! it was nice to be treated with care and attention to my needs. from the er where it all started with a friendly staff, although the wait was loooooooong, to the post-op stay of 5 days where the medical staff was very accommodating, courteous and caring. all my questions were answered by the pros and i did not freak out of being stuck in a hospital during this coronavirus crisis. adventhealth has been remodeling their hospitals and i was super blessed to get a brand new spanking room. it felt good to see how clean and comfy it was with all the state of art goodies. my only disappointment was at discharge because it took forever and the post-op meals which were not supposed to be solid food after a gallbladder removal...always educate yourself by researching guys, ignorance is not bliss when it comes to health...but i don't blame the nursing staff for that i blame the doctors because they're the ones giving the orders. but i must say they respected my input and made the proper changes to my diet.
overall, i do recommend this adventhealth hospitals  for your medical needs. now, to recover and change the way i eat!

if there was less than one star for rating, i would not rate them a 1! i recently took my wife to providence northeast er after over 2 hours of severe abdominal pain at home. i was not allowed to go in due to covid 19. a wheelchair was needed for her to get into the building due to the amount of pain she was experiencing. she was wheeled into the er waiting area and left alone. then staff called her to the window...no one offered to assist. she struggled to get to the window bent over in pain in the wheelchair. she provided the information and was triaged. her blood pressure was much higher than typical and she attempted to tell the staff. they handed her a urine specimen cup and told her when she could provide a sample to bring it back up to them...and again no assistance to someone doubled over in a wheelchair. she texted me and we left to seek care elsewhere. the following day a physician told us never to go the providence ne for any reason due to substandard care. when i returned to work, a number of colleagues told me the same. the substandard care she received was appalling and should never happen to anyone.

my son cut his face and i called medcheck. teresa answered and was professional and kind. we went and there was a 5  minute wait. my son was in and the staff was outstanding. they talked to my son and were kind, professional and fun! yes fun, even tho my son had to get stitches. the pa talked my son thru all the steps and we were out the door in no time.

ended up being here longer than expected so i ventured to the lobby for starbucks and then to the cafe on the 3rd floor.  bunless burger and fries.  all cooked fresh and the burger is flame grilled.  delicious and inexpensive! $5 burger and $1 fries.

as a seasoned health care professional, i can spot incompetence, laziness or lack of empathy a mile away. i didn't find any of the above at pomerado hospital. in fact, quite the contrary. the doctors, nurses, ancillary staff, and every professional who took care of mom were absolutely outstanding. i could not have been more impressed. they nailed her diagnosis, missed nothing and expedited the right treatment in the most compassionate way. cheryl and dr. marzack in the er, dr. baswani, catherine, n.p. and ashley, rn on 4 east and others were literal life savers. sam at the front door? a ++. they epitomize excellence in clinical medicine. god bless them all. we will be forever grateful. don't be afraid to seek treatment at this hospital. it is extremely clean and they are very careful. mom is 91 so we were afraid to take her in because of covid, but it was perfectly fine and she is so much better now! thank you, palomar hospital!

if i could give negative stars i would. every experience i have had at this hospital is atrocious.

my daughter spiked a high fever (above 104) with a slight cough, lethargy, loss of appetite, drooling, stomach pain, bloat and gas. we brought her in to the hospital since it was 1am and we were frightened it might be something serious.

they put us in the covid area and quarantined us. the doctor barely looked at her. checked her ears and mouth and vitals and sent us on our way! no covid test, no urine analysis.. she didn't even exam my child's abdominal or body at all.

how is this standard practice!? this place is employed by clowns.

such an incompetent hospital! i went in about 3 weeks ago to er because i had covid-19 symptoms, they rufused to test me because i didn't have a fever, tested me for the flu (which came back negative) and told me i was good to go back to work 2 days later. 

guess what? after spreading it to my entire household, my brother went into er with severe symptoms and tested positive for the coronavirus. great job guys, your incompetence not only gave my entire family coronavirus, but i almost went back to work and infected more people as well! thankfully my common sense told me i shouldn't go even though the nurses and doctors said it was fine.

this place is a joke. my 1 1/2 year old son went in because he had a seizure due to a high fever. paramedics said to keep his clothes off to keep him cool. they stuck my wife in a hall way with small dividers separating her from people that were actually coughing. my son had no other symptoms, so where is the logic putting a small child that just had a seizure in a hall way with people coughing. not to mention there was no safety/ sanitation procedure in place. so we left and went to children's. if your going to quarantine people you should do so by level of risk. the. you have the audacity  to call and tell us that you could neither confirm nor deny that anyone tested positive for covid and if we wanted to get tested you would expedite testing!!! so we were concerned about covid before and now even more so with your lack of sanitation and common sense. i will never go to this place again. do not bring your children here. it's sad when other medical professionals can agree that your a joke.

my son had spiked a fever and had a febrile seizure a couple nights ago. i've never experienced that with any of my other children before, so i was terrified. we called paramedics and they told us we can take him to the hospital since it's 5 minutes from our house and they felt he was okay, just maybe have him monitored. when i arrived i checked him in and told them what happened, and since he had a fever they said they needed to rule out covid so they sent us to the designated area for people displaying covid symptoms, which is a little hall with chairs along the wall and small barriers between them that really aren't protecting you from anything. i stood there carrying my frightened son (who was only in a diaper as the paramedics said we should keep him that way to help cool him- and won't wear a mask because he's 1 and a half) for well over an hour around three coughing adults. i was told 3 times within that time frame that my son had a room and they were coming to get us. i ended up walking out of there and driving all the way to children's where he was seen much faster. oh, he was negative for covid there. so thank you for potentially exposing my baby and myself and having absolutely no compassion.

probably by far the worst er experience my husband and i have ever been through. my husband broke his leg and so we took him to this nice looking hospital thinking it would be better than tri-city hospital, boy were we wrong. i took him there at 1 pm, i couldn't stay with him because of the corona virus, so i waited in the car, he had to wait until 7 pm to see the dr. and get his leg taken care of, meanwhile he was freezing, thirsty, hungry and in an extreme amount of pain and no one would help him, do not go to this er/hospital unless you like waiting forever and want to suffer!!! we will never go back!

i wanted to take a few minutes to say thank you to the whole banner thunderbird staff. let me start off by saying, i was incredibly nervous, as it was my first time being admitted, having an iv and being put under. and, with covid, doing it without a visitor. 

it started the day before with an extremely informative phone call from admissions asking questions and giving great direction on where to go surgery day.

i checked in, sat a few moments in the waiting room then was checked in. i was escorted back to another waiting room by a gentleman, wish i could remember his name! but he was so pleasant, singing and dancing through the halls. 

i was then brought back to prep, where i was with lizette. she was amazing to say the least. extremely gentle, comforting and communicative, always letting me know what was going on. for my first iv experience, she made it essentially painless. i then met with the anesthesiologist, wish i got his name. very helpful and friendly. then, cody came in, the surgical nurse. she was also very assuring and kind. dr. matlock was also very kind, as always! she was assuring through the whole process, even before surgery day. takes the time to answer any questions and you never feel rushed speaking with her. lastly, after surgery, i woke up to sandra and michelle. i dont recall meeting sandra before, i think she was in the or? mustve been the anesthesia! michelle though, i cant say enough about her! so sweet and caring when i woke up. got me whatever i asked for and was willing to be there with me the whole time til i felt comfortable getting up. 

all in all, a great experience in a weird time we are in. the hospital was organized, cautious and still very caring. thank you for easing the mind of this big baby! :)

i feel compelled to write this review as i genuinely feel that this hospital has some of the best, most compassionate nurses and doctors in the country. it's devastating enough to have a relative admitted to a hospital in the best of times. during a covid pandemic, it's absolutely heartbreaking as even your closest friends and family members are unable to be there with you to help you through things. my grandmother was recently admitted to glens falls hospital and the staff has been nothing short of fantastic. dr. cleaver has been in daily contact with my father, providing him with updates on her condition. then i spoke to the most amazing nurse on t3 who immediately put my mind at ease (she got my grandmother to eat and take her meds- which in itself is an epic feat!)  and she arranged for a facetime chat with my grandmom when she is feeling up to it. they are just beyond compassionate and helpful and fantastic during this horrible time and i am so grateful to have them taking care of grandmom right now. so thank you dr. cleaver and the awesome nurses from t3 who are taking care of her! you are so appreciated!

i have been hospitalized several times in the last six months, due to chronic lupus complications, and can say that i have received excellent care from the medical/surgical unit staff during each stay (a total of 30+ days,) even during my most recent admission this month, as the staff work under the increased anxiety and fears of the covid-19 pandemic.

i can say that, to a person, the staff were efficient, patient, kind, and attentive. i never sensed any staff member was as exhausted and/or overwhelmed as they must be feeling. in fact, the night of my most recent admission i was aware that the swing-shift staff were still on the unit long after the night shift began, but they remained attentive and caring, never making me feel as though they couldn't wait for me to get settled in so they could leave.

i must also give praise to the support staff of cna's (talk about having the "patience of a saint!",) housekeepers, kitchen staff, etc. the young woman who came in to clean my room each day was always smiling, in a lovely mood, and always wished me well as she left my room. i only wish i could remember her name so i could acknowledge her personally!

during this crazy, scary, and uncertain time we are all living in right now, i hope we all keep in mind that the personnel at our medical facilities are just as fallible and human as those of us who are seeking their care; they have families, homes, and loved ones to care for as well. under any circumstances, the care i've received these past several months would be considered great... under current circumstances, i can only say, "thank you all for the excellent care you have provided!"

this review is primarily for customer service. 

great staff in person who made me feel comfortable & taken care of in the er. there were times the nurse & doctor apologized they were "sidetracked" & kept me waiting. 

however, the staff who assists over the phone is rude, shows no empathy & very impatient. i called today (06/15/2020 at 1:18pm pst) regarding a prescription a doctor prescribed me. the pharmacy said they needed the doctors approval so i called the hospital. the response from the receptionist was "well i don't know who your doctor is" and "okkaaayyyy". very unprofessional, unhelpful & rude; especially during these times (covid19) where patients & people in need should receive compassion. my prescription is critical for my health, without it i can have a severe infection. fortunately i am an emotionally stable person. however i worry about people like my mother calling who would be treated with disrespect & provided with no help & only with attitude. thought it was healthcare.

in my 31 years of life i've never been on the receiving end of any hospital care or services, during a pandemic nonetheless. even amidst what people would describe as chaos within healthcare centers, i received the highest level of care and attention. these healthcare workers really made me feel taken care of and safe after enduring a multi bone injury right in the middle of the covid-19 outbreak. after being taken to the er and being told i broke 2 bones and would need surgery i for sure thought i was going to be out on a list since in ca surgeries were told to have been put on hold so that all workers can focus on covid-19 related cases, but no i was told i'd be worked on within 24 hours. from the time i was admitted to the time i was discharged i can't think of one instance when things could have been better. where i don't suggest you find yourself in a hospital at all other than giving birth to a child, if you're going to be like me and wait 31 years for your first injury i highly suggest you take yourself to memorial hospital within dignity health's network of centers. thanks for taking care of me!

without writing a long essay (which i did and sent it to dignity health and the hospital), when i simply asked to call my sister and leave this place ama, the attitude of the entire floor went from accommodating to mistreatment. these people should never be allowed to treat humans or animals. if i had the option, i'd leave no stars. with covid19 so prominent, i was not allowed visitors or contact with my sister until i asked to leave. they fully abused me and probably all patients on the floor. with no visitors allowed, they fully took advantage of that. they were cruel and fully intended to 'teach me a lesson.' further, a few of the pt workers were also mistreating me. upon leaving, two women who i have never seen before looked at me and said, "there's the shit stirrer." what? how did they figure this? the only 'shit' i stirred was asking to leave. i was called names, told they didn't 'like me,' and was accused of coming in for an overdose. which was patently ridiculous. i went in for a recurring issue. listen to the negative reviewers. don't fall for that whole 'they rock' attitude. they don't. stay away from this hospital at all costs.

this is a review for their labor and delivery part of the hospital.

i'm currently writing this in the recovery room, having just delivered my second baby (first one with el camino, first was with ucsf in the city). i just wanted to use this moment to rave about my experience this time around compared to ucsf.

from triage to l&d to recovery, all the doctors and nurses here are by far the most experienced, kind, knowledgeable and kind people i have ever met. due to covid i never got a chance to do a hospital tour, so i had no idea what to expect when i checked in 2 nights ago after laboring for 24h at home.

at triage i was greeted by nurse melissa, who checked me and i hadn't progressed enough to be admitted. instead of just sending me home, she asked me to walk the hallway for 1h to see if it'll speed things up. and it did, i went from 3cm to 5cm during that hour and was admitted right after.

the rest of the nursing team were all super pleasant, knowledgeable and explained every little thing to me without me having to ask. there's a really positive energy and rapport between the nurses so it carries through the whole bedside manner. my iv drip at ucsf last time was a traumatic experience, they couldn't find my vein and blood kept spurting everywhere. this time at el camino, they had a nurse who specialized in iv insertion and she did it painlessly and perfectly in one to without any blood. 

i knew i wanted an epidural this time, and instead of dictating to me when i should get it, they told me to tell them whenever i wanted it. i decided to walk for another hour before asking for the epidural. now let's talk a bit about the epidural. i had dr. k (forget the full name) and he was so good. no pain, super calm, and the meds took effect almost immediately. with ucsf i was in so much pain and the injection didn't even work the first time, i had to wait 2h for the anesthesiologist to come back to up my dosage. this time, the dosage was perfect because i had no pain but eventually i could feel the pressure as i was nearing 10cm. i could move my legs and could feel the pressure of contractions so my pushing was super effective. i'm told this is the perfect dosage and that the doctor is really good.

now onto the pushing phase. at ucsf (since it's a teaching hospital) there were 10+ people in the room while i was pushing. some were helping while others were just spectating. this time, i had one nurse stay with me the whole time helping me push, and once it got to a certain point she called my ob and she came and took it to the finish line. hardly tore, got 2 stitches and no hemorrhages. i tore second degree and hemorrhaged pretty badly with my first.

once baby was here, they moved us to the mother & baby section. since the epidural wore off rather quickly i was able to pee way faster than with my first, and the nurses in recovery were all super nice and accommodating. i also had a fabulous lactation consultant help me with breastfeeding, who really gave me the most helpful pointers that i never got with my first. when i was at ucsf with my first, i had a lot of pain in latching and the lc there told me that nothing was wrong and a "little" pain is normal. basically made me feel like a wuss. turned out my firstborn had a tongue tie and lip tie but i didn't get that diagnosed til she was already 3mo. of course by then my breastfeeding journey was already a hot mess and did not go well at all. the lc at el camino (stacey was her name) took her time to teach me how to latch and basically said that proper breastfeeding should never hurt. after 30min of training i was able to find a good latch and now my baby is breastfeeding really well. night and day.

anyways, i just wanted to take the time to give credit to an incredible group of staff. it's seriously night and day to my experience at ucsf and i wouldn't have known unless i had something to compare against. 

thank you for such a pleasant birthing experience. i never knew i would ever use "pleasant" to describe labor and delivery.

if i could, i would put negative stars. i'd go to a vet before i'd go to baptist main on kendall drive! 
     saturday march 28th my boyfriend noticed (when he woke up) that i seemed confused, was slurring my words, talking strangely, and appeared off balance ( previous stroke in my history). also had radiating chest pain and a blood producing cough. i have tons of health issues so he was pretty concerned.
      we went to baptist urgent care at 137th and 152nd street. everyone at this facility was wonderful! i was triaged and sped into a treatment area very quickly, and saw the doctor within 10 minutes. ekg, blood work, iv in place, tested for flu/ covid19, and evaluated amazingly fast. the doctor decided i needed to go to baptist main on kendall drive. we chose the expediency of driving there. i was still a little out of it, so my boyfriend was providing most of the info. the caregivers at urgent care kept him away from everyone, but close enough to answer questions.
      when we got to the main hospital, things just went downhill. we pulled up to the door and a nurse told him to just drop me off and they would call him. we tried to convey the reasoning for him to remain but were ignored. an orderly came with a wheelchair and asked why i was there. i tried to explain, but he said " really? cause you look fine!". 
     registered at the desk and was put in a room. guy from registration came in to get my info and for me to sign consent. i was wearing a mask the whole day up to this time. not one person at this point had one on. the registration gentleman brought over my papers to sign, and began flipping the various forms for me by licking his finger! no wonder there's have been confirmed cases at this hospital! 
     then, doctor micheal mai came in, he was masked and gloved.  but as soon as he spoke, i knew nothing was going to get better. i called my boy friend as planned, so he could voice his observations. we were both talked over, the symptoms down played, and he too said "you don't look sick now, though." we were both adamant that this wasn't something to brush off with all of my health problems. in an exasperated tone, we were told " to make us happy he'd run every test under the sun" . when he left my room, he began talking in an extremely loud voice and said ( there were other patients in the rooms on that hall) '" we'll run everything, to rule out the nothing that's wrong with her". 
     at that point i called the nurse (yiska) and asked for ama papers. the nurse also said i looked and sounded fine. three doctors! how lucky was i? i signed the papers and left. 
     to add insult to injury, security and the nurses at the door refused to give me the patient advocate number without explaining to them why i felt i needed it. 
     i've never been treated like a  hypochondriac, especially since they knew nothing about my medical history. total disregard for me as a patient with those inherent rights you hear about totally ignored, as well as contempt when a snap decision on their part was contested. i will assure you, not only will i and my loved ones never patronize this hospital, but i will be posting on social media and  by word of mouth how horribly i was treated. never again.

what happened felt unehtical and like medical blackmail. our only other option was to contest it with medicare and be on the hook for the bill for that time in the hospital past the premature discharge. so now she's in rehab (against her wishes but our best option under these circumstances) until we can get home health care set up because any money that we do have should be reserved for making her better, not fighting the grim reaper and his games.

it is my hope that action would be taken to prevent what happened to us during these uncertain and stressful times from happening to another family having their baby at froedtert.

these things make the good people at froedtert look bad. nurses on l&d like corey and becky as well as those on the 6th floor including india, robyn, kelsey, and nikki as well as lactation consultants like wanda and pediatricians like dr. francis or franklin (she had red hair) and her male resident from australia. these professionals helped to balance out our experience, but i'm hoping my email to the 6th floor manager & this review might save others the heartache and stress froedtert caused us in a time that is supposed to be joyful, happy, and most of all, safe.

i have some sort of mystery sickness and was advised by my doc to go to an emergency room and since qotv was the closest one, there i went.
i'll list the good/okay points first:
evening parking was good, we got there after 8pm on a wednesday.
check-in was quick and the social distancing was observed by seating everyone outside in tents.
the wait time was in the middle. it took a couple of hours to get everything done and i could get out of there. wasn't the fastest, considering there weren't that many patients around, but it wasn't the slowest.
the nurse conducting the usual tests was doing her job. 
the doc that gave me the "diagnosis" did a job.
the check out nurse was really nice and helped me get up from the bench, which was a plus.

on to the not-so-good points:
i was having trouble standing but there was no place to sit when i was filling out the entry paperwork.
the nurse performing the initial blood tests and temp checks had a oral thermometer. of course it had those little sanitary sleeves, but this place doesn't have any of those non-touch forehead temperature sensors? during an epidemic? 
the doc came out and made a very general diagnosis and gave me some prescriptions. other than the covid-19, there were no other tests mentioned to figure out what i had. when i asked for the hospital to fax the information to my primary care doc, he replied that "they didn't have that technology." ... what?!  i haven't heard of a fax being called technology in a loong while. no wonder they don't have those other types of thermometers. i wonder how they communicate information, via smoke signals?
when the final nurse came out to give me the check out paperwork & prescriptions he said i could check on my test results via an online portal, color me surprised by that news. how is a place that doesn't have fax technology have a website portal. not very consistent this place.
okay, here it is days later and i feel less like death. i want to check my test results, so i try going to the link. first off let me say the "link" they provided is ridiculously long: https://portal.emanatehealth.org/templates/selfsignup-quvweb.livef-en-us.html 
most people access the internet on their phones, so i can't even imaging how frustrating it must be to type this crap into the address bar and don't even think about making a typo because it won't work if you do.
i tried logging into their online portal multiple times on three separate browsers with zero success. so i guess qotv's "website portal" is more in line with the level of tech savvy one would expect from a place that doesn't have fax technology.
no worries, i'll just call in (and probably get put on perpetual hold or never reach a human which would be par for course) and see if i can get my information that way.

over all, i'm not impressed by this place, but it's not the worst i've seen... but we are talking about the american healthcare "system" so the bar is set pretty low. 

i came in, got some medications which helped a lot and the staff were on average okay, so win- i guess. i don't know what i'm going to do if i get any more strange sicknesses that a doc just can't throw some meds at. hopefully i won't and that's the best anyone (who isn't rich and/or has amazing health care insurance) can hope for.

2. the doctor told me she seemed to be okay and recommended i come back if the symptoms get worse or continue... thats the reason i was sent in the first place.
3. the hospital discharge papers had the wrong reason for the visit, and instructions.. 
the staff was nice, but didn't seem like my daughter received quality care other than a visual inspection, no further tests. they took good precaution regulating and controlling er flow during this pandemic.

i'm very disappointed with the er medical staff at mercy gilbert. i've heard all great things about them. however when i was checked in at this hospital on tuesday, march 24, i had a completely different experience. 

it all started when i was told by the covid 19 hotline, that i could go to the banner urgent care on higley, to get tested. i waited a good hour before getting called back. (no it wasn't busy) appointment was @ 11:30, i checkin 11:15, called by 12:16pm. once i entered the back room, my legs gave out on me and i ended up collapsing. the nurse helped me to the room and onto the bed. at this point my fever was 102.6 and my body started to have convulsions. the banner urgent care called 911 and i was sent to this hospital. i wasn't tested  for covid 19 with banner urgent care.

i was asked a list of questions by the emt about where i work and have i traveled lately. told them i was a flight attendant based in jfk/nyc. also told them i started experiencing symptoms on monday night march 23. during this time my body was in so much pain and i had this excruciating headache unlike nothing i felt before in my life. 

we quickly arrived (which felt like forever) and i was taken to a room where i was met by er dr. kent first,  then by nurse rene a little later. and i was asked again the same list of questions from each. i just wanted to pop my head off from body at this point because the pain was so unbearable. 

here is where everything went downhill. 
dr.kent said she was going to run a flu and strep test on me. i asked her what will happen when they came back negative. (which i knew were both negative because i have had the flu and strep before and my body has never reacted like this, plus i got the flu shot back in october 2019).

dr. kent became very short with me and slightly raised her voice and seemed very irritated because i wanted to know about getting tested for covid 19 (which the next day my doctor now tested me and i was indeed positive). she was so concerned about state regulations and not admitting me to the hospital, that she sent me home with antibiotics after my xrays showed i had  community-acquired pneumonia and i was told i could return back to work after 3 days if symptoms improved. and when she told me about the pneumonia, dr. kent stood by the curtain and quickly walked away. really?!? 

so i knew something was off with my body and this was not normal, i don't have any underlying health issues. never in my 10 years of flying as a flight attendant have i had pneumonia. i'm in my early 30s and pretty healthy. i went to my doctor now and nurse john shipp was the only one who believed me enough to test me on wednesday, march 25, and by friday (yes two days later) i had a video chat with my doctor now and was positive for covid 19. later on that day i ended up collapsing yet once again experiencing hypoxia (lack of oxygen to the brain) and was admitted to banner baywood hospital. where i spent the next 6 days on antibiotics, blood thinners, and malaria medication hydroxychloroquine. 
if it wasn't for me taking the initiative to find help, i more than likely wouldn't be here today and my child would be motherless.

i have never had  bad experience there. went there for stomach pain. of course with this virus going on things were a little different. they were not busy but seemed that things were a little slower that usual. they had  light staff so that was the reason i'm sure.  all in all i got taken care and and everyone was nice and friendly.

on january 15,2020 i entered palos hospital by way of their emergency department and all of the excellent care that i received during my subsequent visit was initiated at that entry point... i ended up being diagnosed with a life threatening diagnosis.. from the emergency room to the imaging dept . physicians, interventional radiology department, any necessary transports, icu, coronary stepdown unit, dietary, chaplain services the expertise and delivery of care was superb. having worked in the medical field for over fifty years i can base my opinion on lots of knowledge of medical cares... i had limited and vague preconceptions regarding palos hospital prior to my recent stay... at this point in time i obviously cannot express enough gratitude to all involved in my care... after this very delayed thanku i have expressed to palos hospital that i not only received excellent care but it was delivered by personnel that seemed as if they had all taken what i would call.. "the disney approach" during their delivery of services

came to the er with massive stomach pain & they had me wait outside under a tent and asked my husband to wait in the car (well organized to minimize covid spreading ).  i was nervous about coming to the hospital due to covid, let alone a smaller hospital.. but

when they took me in, er nurse jose, was extremely kind & attentive.  i don't think i could've gotten through the pain without his help.  fortunately got scheduled for surgery an hour later, underwent appendectomy bc my appendix ruptured, and am now under the care of multiple nurses (kamal, raymond, & tina) who have all been great.  i think they'll let me go home as soon as i pass gas.

thank you for all your help!

always great service here..i was honestly scared to go to hospital because of this corona virus stuff going on.but they definitely doing a great job keeping everything clean and safe.was in and out in about a hour and a half.keep up the good work guys

although i received excellent care at the hospital, the billing practices are quite fraudulent.  when you are admitted to have your hospital procedure, you are taken into the admissions office and told how much it will cost you.  but if you choose to pay right then, they will give you a discount! which is a lie as they are only quoting you an estimated amount.  they are not saving you a dime.

so beware - do not give these people any money prior to your procedure.

review:
*do not go to this hospital!* their er staff is unprofessional, rude and has no empathy whatsoever. if i could give it 0 stars i would. i don't even know how this place is still operating. arrived at 6 am with a severe strep throat that is spreading to my ear. i could not swallow, talk and was weak from not eating. 

when we arrived there no one in the waiting room. and no one in the lobby greeting area. my fiancé then had to bang on the glass to get someone's attention after waiting 40 minutes with no greeting, no paperwork. then a lady arrived and she instructed us to wait outside because apparently strep throat could be corona virus. i was compliant and went outside in the cold with my fiancé. 30 minutes later a nurse comes outside to take vitals and instructs us to wait for the doctor who has to screen me before i am allowed inside. mind you i had no fever or other corona symptoms. the nurses knew i was in extreme pain. i waited outside for 1.5 hours and was never seen by the doctor!! my fiancé had to yell through the electric doors for someone to pay attention to us... he was ignored for a while but kept trying to get their attention. after getting the attention of one of the staff he let them know if they could find out how much longer we would have to wait to be seen by the doctor for just a screening not even for treatment - to which the staff responded "you can leave if you want to!" with a very rude and uncaring attitude. my fiancé and i were shocked by the staff laughing, cracking jokes and completely ignoring their patients. i could have gotten better customer service at walmart or the dmv....

after flagging down and crying from pain in front of the nurse she finally claimed there was a glitch in the system and that the doctor could not see me until the "computer was working". yet they were treating patients that got their after i arrived. i ended up leaving and going to culver city urgent care right down the street. they provided excellent care in less than 30 min. they staff at urgent care all told me that they would never recommend this place to any of their patients... if only i had known before i got there. if you value your health and customer service don't step foot in this place. i work in healthcare and i am extremely disappointed. 

they clearly don't care about the reviews. from what i see they gave you a fake email and phone number just to pretend like they care but the hundreds of negative reviews say otherwise!

review:
if i could i'd give a -0¹!!!!
don't let any of your loved ones visit, stay, or even pass by this place! my brother recently passed on "june 21st" and the reason for quotations is i think he was gone days before. there's an incompassionate and extremely unprofessional "nurse" there by the name of grace who tells any and all people any information about a patient they want want to know about! when grace called to tell my mother that my brother was "code blue" and they were working in him said says "ok i gotta go back in there bye" then just hung up and my mom calls her back and she just says "oh i'm sorry momma he passed we tried" then hung up! as we, my mother and i were crying cause we just lost my brother i started getting messages from family with their condolences i'm like how does everyone know we havent gotten around to making any calls with tears coming out our eyes and boogers coming out our noses! how? so i called june 22nd because i wanted to speak to a supervisor or the one on the highest pedestal regarding some questions, concerns & complaints so they transferred me to "supervisor ray morales" whom is in my opinion as incompetent as the janitor pretending to be a doctor in fact it may have been for all i know. i asked him "about grace and her giving just anybody information about a patients condition who isn't immediate family" he made that sound you make when "you get caught or the jig is up" i said also all the information that grace was giving us "is fishy" i said "honestly i think my brother was gone a lot sooner than the day we were told, i think my brother died a week ago and that's why grace was telling us we had 30 minutes to get there to see his body cause you guys took him out the freezer to thaw a little bit so we can see him so you van throw him back in the freezer!" and he said nothing. no denial, no defense no answers for me none! he just informed me to call the hospital number with extension 333 (satans son's number?) to speak to "quality assurance" i'm like "is that like the surveys to say how you did?" (with sarcasm) he said "it's to let them know you weren't satisfied"  are u kidding me!!! if i'm not satisfied were they gonna give us back my brother or a coupon for 2 for 1??!!! a free hamburger perhaps ‍!? my brother was a life and he mattered to a lot of people not just another "covid-19" count!! my brother went to kaiser in baldwin park on june 11th cause he had trouble swallowing, he did have diabetes and "dysphagia" is a common complication of diabetes. at kaiser there's all kinds of tents outside because no one can go in due to covid-19 so you wait outside and they take your temperature and vitals outside my brother had no fever, no cough so eventually they take him in and tell his girlfriend she can't go in so she's like ok call me when your done as we live a few blocks away he says "ok" and he goes in. she talks to him a few hrs later he said they were gonna give him an mri cause he said "they don't know what's wrong with him and he didnt have covid-19" his girlfriend is like "ok well call and keep me updated" he said "ok"  my brother got transferred to los angeles community hospital and when he got there they told him he they were gonna give him another mri and something about taking spinal fluid then they told him he had covid-19 so he calls his girlfriend crying "come pick me up they're saying i have that sh**!" he was scared and alone!!! utterly alone! there is more to this review but they have a limit to rewiews!

review: i went in for shoulder surgery, and was concerned about doing it during the covid 19 crisis.  i had a great experience. i was screened immediately when i entered the hospital for the covid virus.b the front desk admin folks were true professionals.  the nurses, doctors and others who gave me treatment from prr-surgery, the actual surgery, and the recovery phase we're all very caring and professional in giving me the best care possible. i highly recommend this hospital over the large, corporate hospitals.  best decision i've ever made.

my doctor referred me to elmhurst's "covid hotline" and when i dialed, a woman who said is a nurse but "not a practicing nurse" by the name lisa wasted no time to dismiss me claiming (i quote) "if you can talk, you don't have covid-19". that happened despite being referred by my doctor who thought my symptoms were consistent with covid-19. i tried to explain to this "non-practicing nurse" that since i got sick, 10 days ago, one day i may feel better (like today) but next it can be worse than any other day, consistent with another peculiarity of the illness. i tried to press her about my doctor wanting me to get tested, she told me to find another place that will test anyone (aka even those who are obviously fine, by elmhurst standards). or that she could transfer my call to another team but warned me that if she didn't believe i had anything, the other team was going to be even harder to convince (at this point i was wondering whether i was trying to get tested or was i competing for a top corporate job) in summary, this hotline's main job is to deny tests.

at the end, this "non practicing nurse" told me i probably had some other bug and "good luck with your symptoms". edit: glad i couldn't get out of bed, otherwise i would have infected who knows how many people, since i was running errands for others.

edit: my physician contested their decision and they gave in. they called me to schedule a test and it was done 4/24. it was another contentious call (things got rough when i asked what made them change their mind) but this time they called me. looks like having to backpedal on their original decision was insulting (where else have i seen that? something to do with briefings, ovals and offices...).

edit: on 4/25 results came in, i tested positive. tested positive. tested positive for covid-19.

edit: 5/1 they now call me pretty often because i tested positive. i ask them now and then if they still deny tests to people who can talk but they refuse to speak about it. "that was then, this is now" said a nurse during one of the tracing phone calls. such question seems to hit a nerve.

review: this was my first time admitted to this hospital in corvallis.  i arrived at the er with labored breathing, high fever and severe coughing.  the staff was amazing.  they were so gentle and kind.  because they needed to test me for covid-19 i was isolated and couldn't have family near me.  the nurses became my family and were so very kind.  fortunately, i didn't have covid-19 and was treated for a severe case of pneumonia.  i was in the hospital a total of 5 days and only had kind, caring nurses and informative and gentle doctors.  they truly were angels during a very scary traumatic experience.

labor and delivery department nurses are wonderful. 

i've been anxious while checking-in as my family was not able to stay with me at the hospital due to covid-19 - kids under 12 years old are not allowed so we agreed that my husband will stay at home with our daughter as we didn't know how soon i will deliver the baby and be discharged. 

ashley was the first (night) nurse i met and she made me feel so comfortable and relaxed, she was very caring, she helped me whenever i needed something and supported me when there've been any doubts. 

natashia and vick did a great job during the day hours. 

and finally, channel was the nurse who assisted with the baby delivery, she's amazing! she coached me, and cared for me, and inspired me when i had no more power to proceed. 

when the baby was born she's been placed skin-to-skin on me and she was checked by the doctors right there, we stayed together for a rather long wonderful time before she was taken to that baby-table for weight check and the shot. nurses reminded me and took many photos for me to share with the family. 

i never felt lonely during my stay at the labor and delivery department and received an excellent care. i am very grateful for that to each person whom i met there.

marie was the night nurse at the mother and baby department and i felt at home with her too. she was a great help and so passionate! 

i would like to mention how quick and easy was the process of baby vital documents submission, the lady was great at gathering correctly all the information by phone (we have not so simple names and last names, you know :)). by the way, no issues this time - we received them all soon by mail. 

the meal services were so kind to check with me several times if i really didn't want anything as they 'saw' that i was getting late with the discharge from the hospital. 

it was a great experience. many thanks to everyone involved!

review:
labor and delivery team 04/02/20 - 04/04/20

i gave birth to my daughter crystalli rose one week ago and had to share our stay while in kaiser. as a first time mom and having to give birth during covid 19 of course i had so many worries and fears. i was pleasantly surprised with how calm, clean and attentive everyone was. from hard working cleaners, maintenance workers administrators, food handlers, nurses and doctors. i felt completely safe and well taken care of. 

i wish i had a kept track of every single nurse and doctor by full name or id number but here are a few that really went above and beyond.

04/02/20: dr. nelson and rn debbie explained every treatment and made sure i was as comfortable and cleaned up as possible. 

04/03/20: aipang was very attentive checking in with me every strong contraction and when my daughters heart rate kept dropping she told me her recommendations and got the approval from the doctor immediately to keep my baby closely monitored. aipang made sure i ate, had juice and stayed active to help prep my body for the next stage of labor. when i finally reached my pain limit and asked her opinion on when to get the epidural she reassured me now was the time and called to have that prepared. 

within minutes the anesthesiologist kevin was there! he was very good at explaining the process to me and coached me to relax my body before placing the epidural. he gave me breaks in between the most intense contractions and checked on me in 20 minutes to make sure i was okay and feeling better! i was able to get sleep, drink fluids and still move around in bed but was numb in all the right places.

04/04/20: rn liz was very sweet and attentive. we had great conversations as see took care of me. when ever my daughters heart rate would dropped she would help me position myself another way and that happened many times. during my active labor she was extremely compassionate and helped me get through my contractions and pain management.  before i knew it it was time to start pushing! she was fantastic explaining and coaching me to push properly. which i greatly appreciated since i was pretty numb down there. 

dr. fernandez explained me options to help assist my delivery. i was scared, exhausted and feeling overwhelmed but she gave me her opinion and understood my wishes( no episiotomy) 

rn velvet was wonderful teaching my husband and i how to feed, hold, burp, clean and bathe our. velvet worked with us to get discharged and back home as quickly as possible. she gave us formula to help the baby urinate and we were finally headed home. our daughter was born completely safe and healthy thanks to the amazing team at kaiser santa clara's l&d department!!

background: my dad struggled with congenital heart disease as well as a number of other health issues. in april 2019, he ended up in van ness cpmc to get the lvad. there were multiple complications with the surgery, was in the icu, and survived. it was a miracle that he survived that. two months of his recovery was spent here, and went to another hospital after. fast forward to a few weeks ago. he was hospitalized again and was brought to the icu once more. he passed away and due to the pandemic, we were unable to be with him.

our experience:
me, my three sisters, and mom spent every day at icu during my dad's first visit. my mom has been an rn for the last 30 years at a nearby hospital (and a damn good one at that)  and was deeply concerned for the quality of care he was receiving. most of the staff was quite friendly, but wouldn't follow through on their promises. so, we found ourselves assisting our dad to make up for a majority of the nurses' lack of help (will list reasons why later). second time, it was strictly phone communication with both my dad and staff. we were faced with similar issues again.  

concerns:
(first hospitalization)
- staff, both nurses and doctors, would set up meetings for updates and would hardly ever be on time, nonetheless show up  
- would promise phone call updates without delivery
- lack of patient care: wouldn't turn him regularly, my mom had to do it
- during intubation, found that his trach site had puss and was smelly, indicating they weren't cleaning him properly. we addressed this, and found it was infected
- during his approx. 1 month of intubation, they kept him on restraints constantly which put even more stress on my dad.  even when there weren't any ivs to pull out, no trach, they still restrained him, adding onto my dad's restlessness
- nurse practitioner was trying to send my dad home without rehab, even though he was clearly imbalanced and was in no condition to leave 

(second hospitalization) 
- dad was put on npo in preparation for multiple tests, but staff would regularly reschedule his tests. he literally wasn't eating ever because of this 
- ****we had a half hour discussion with the nurse practitioner via phone call to discuss our concerns including that my dad was lactose intolerant and shouldn't be given ensure, and that my dad did not want to be intubated anymore. she said "oh, wow, i will have a meeting tomorrow with the staff about this" on a friday then found out my dad was intubated on sunday night. we did not receive that information until monday at 3pm by the doctor. when we told him about our discussion with the nurse practitioner, he said he didn't know that.****** 
- ...and my dad was still given ensure after we mentioned lactose intolerance. 
- my dad passed away the next day and we were told by the nurse we would "receive a phone call" regarding 1) autopsy, 2) what to do with his lvad, 3) results to his bone marrow biopsy immediately because he might have had tuberculosis. we didn't hear anything. my dad's physician who is not apart of van ness cpmc was the one to tell us he had tb and for me and my mom to get tested since we were exposed. 
- on his death certificate, they put the wrong date of hospitalization and apparently, there was no autopsy at all, despite my mom's request??

  
this hospital has some serious work to do on their organization, communication, and ethics. although the runt of our interactions were with the nurses, this is an issue that the hospital must tackle as a whole. it was a deeply saddening experience to witness my dad's condition from beginning to end, especially being unable to advocate for him by his side during the pandemic. i can only imagine how much more stressful this would be for a family that had no medical background. please, please fix this, so other families don't have to go through what we had to go through.

it has been 37 days since i last was able to see my son who is only 62 days old and still in the nicu - all because of a covid visitation policy at texas children's that is excessive, insensitive to parent's/ patient's well-being and out of line with nearly all surrounding hospitals.  37 days i have been prevented from holding him, watching him grow, and having critical moments of bonding.

tch's visitor policy is one parent per stay.  nearly all hospitals for children in medical center have a humane policy of one parent per day (hospitals offering that are children's memorial hermann nicu, harris health ben taub nicu, houston methodist hospital children, shriners hospitals for children) and woman's hospital of texas even allows both parents to visit.   

how is tch so out of line with their competitors? why are they so unsympathetic to the needs of their patient and their families?  

not to mention that the policy itself is illogical - my wife and i live and breathe  in the same household - we represent the same risk factor & germ pool.   i understand limiting the number of visitors in the hospital at any given time, but allowing parents living in the same household to switch daily would not increase the level of statistical risk for the hospital. your intent here was well placed, but the excessive (& out of line) policy that you have drawn is causing harm to parents and preemie babies and without any real benefit.  

so in conclusion tch has a visitation policy that is dramatically more harsh than their peers, that is causing real harm to patients/ their families and doesnt make their patients any more safe.   

i have worked with child advocacy multiple times and spoken to hopsital administrators, they all recognize the policy does not make logical sense but they are either unwilling or incapable to make humane, logical, reasonable accommodations.

review:
in mid-march, just as the covid-19 virus was ramping up, my husband required emergency surgery, not related to covid, for which time was of the essence.  he had initially been taken to st. mary's where it was determined that they didn't have the resources to perform the necessary procedure and he would have to be moved to long beach memorial.  there was no guarantee that he would survive the short trip to receive the procedure. 

he did survive the trip under patrick's care and from the time he arrived at long beach memorial, my mr. received the best care that i could have hoped for.  from the surgical team to the ccu and icu nursing staff, from the nurse practitioners to the physician specialists, the care and professionalism were awesome.  it was apparent that each of the individuals caring for mr. had a personal investment in his recovery.  i was treated with great empathy, was included in the bedside change shift huddles so that i was informed as to what was going on, and any questions i had were answered fully.

because of the virus lock down, i was only able to stay with mr. for a couple of days of his two week stay before i was locked out but was encouraged to call the ccu and icu nursing stations from home for updates.  staff recognized how difficult the separation would be so they also encouraged me to bring his phone to the hospital so that, after mr. awoke, we would be able to communicate, making it a little bit less isolating for him.

i will say that there were a few hiccups at discharge time.  i chalked this up to the fact that mr.'s discharge took place just as non-essential employees were being furloughed and consequently a couple of non-medical things fell through the cracks.  i was pleasantly surprised (and relieved) when i received follow up phone calls from the nurse practitioners for several days following discharge.

i've had aud (alcohol use disorder) for about 40 years. i've tried everything: hypnosis, acupuncture, years on antabuse, 6 months and then 7 years sober in aa in 2000s. each relapse turned into a several weeks long binge, forcing me to seek help again. finally, in 2014 i discovered sinclair method (https://www.the-sinclair-method.com/), which turned out to be a lifesaver. my drinking quickly went down to safe limits and i started to have alcohol free days several times a week. for 5.5 years i was a social drinker, a "normie" in aa speak - until covid struck. 

i live alone, the lockdown made me seriously depressed. all my routines and nearly all social contacts were broken and it felt like a solitary confinement. at some point in april, i stopped taking my medication as prescribed by the sinclair method. from there, my drinking quickly escalated and turned into a heavy 6 weeks binge. by may 13 i had to go to er and then to a 10 days detox in holister; spent the first night in icu nearly having a heart attack. after i got back home on sunday may 24, i wanted to make sure that sinclaire is still working (i still had some meds left from my last refill); i had 3 drinks on the first day, then it went 1, 1, 0, 1, 0 - amazing, considering my condition before the detox. 

in the meantime, my gf discovered the intensive outpatient program (iop) at good sam behavioral. i was surprised to learn that dr cecil a. bradley, who prescribed me naltrexone all these years, is the medical director of this program. the program seemed very useful since a) it is in person, no zoom, b) i got a double diagnosis and could address my underlying emotional issues and c) i could get an extended medical leave, since i was not feeling up to getting back to work immediately. on thursday, may 28 i was there and talked to marcella (admissions) dr khan (sp? md), nurse diane and some other people. i was very open about what i've been doing before, what brought me there and about my intentions (go back on sinclaire, since it works great and aa stopped working for me at some point). everybody seemed to be open-minded, accepting and approving of my course of treatment. some even wrote down the name of my method and said they were curious and want to learn more about it.

thursday and friday sessions were pretty nice, with meditation, some cbt and open discussions on topics suggested by patients themselves. and then, on friday noon dr bradley showed up, took me to his office and told me that their program is based on full abstinence and if i keep up the  controlled drinking, i have to leave. he said there are alternatives to aa and suggested some other program - he just could remember it's name. he is in his 80s and seems to forget things. i promised to think about it over the weekend and tell him about my decision on monday. after all, at this point i could easily refrain from drinking for the duration of the program.

however, on monday my case manager handed me a recovery plan with mandatory conditions: attend at least 3 meetings a week, find a sponsor and report progress at each morning session. i told her i don't do aa, and i was told to go talk to dr bradley, and again he gave me a dilemma: full abstinence and meetings or leave the program. "there is this other program - can't remember it's name... rational recovery?" "- smart recovery?" "- yes, this must be it". "- i researched it, and it has about the same success rate as aa - which is in single digits - whereas sinclair method has success rate near 80%". "- i don't care. this program requires full abstinence and meetings". so i informed him that i'm quitting and went home.

there are several things that really upset and anger me. 
1) why did dr bradley prescribe my medicine all these years and even wrote me another 3 refills on that monday if he disapproves on sinclair method so much? 
2) how does a doctor refer a patient to some program the name of which he can't even remember? does he know anything about it? or he just doesn't care?
3) why did they admit me at all, knowing full well my intentions, knowing dr bradley's views and giving me false hopes? 
4) what kind of doctors put a patient into completely unscientific, faith-based programs with abysmal success rate and force him to abandon something that is proven to work for 80% and this patient in particular?

so i googled dr bradley and discovered that the medical board of california twice has suspended his license, once in 1990 and second time in 2007 (5 years probation). he also was known to be sending referrals to and working at a couple of shady rehabs ran by an uncertified drug addict.

makes you wonder, how does a doctor like cecil bradley ends up a medical director at well-respected hospital like good sam? i would not recommend going to good sam in- or outpatient behavioral programs until they replace him. the rest of staff seems to be ok, but there is nothing they could do to help me under current leadership.

the nightmare continued... i had a great surgeon dr rite- who hold me i'd be discharged the same day as my surgery because i have a compromised immune system and even being in the hospital is a high risk situation for me . they refused to release me, i asked repeatedly to call the dr & explained my situation and the nurses said they'd call the dr but never ever did. i then called the supervisor who said she'd investigate & come see me and she never bothered to do either. i was trapped in y ty here for 12 more hours. i have never ever seen or heard of such aggregious behavior and lack of compassion & disregard for human life. i explained over & over that i'm a chemo patient & it was dangerous to be exposed to covid 19 and the hospital staff displayed a complete disregard for my life - shocking...

early this morning, my sister woke up with intense abdominal pains, trouble breathing, fainting spells, and clammy skin. without hesitation and very concerned for her wellbeing, as any family would be, we called 911, explained her symptoms, and the 911 dispatch sent an ambulance over. she was quickly rushed to the hospital. given the current times and covid-19, we were unable to join her, only able to communicate with her via text message when she was passingly lucid. she began receiving treatment and testing to find the source of the problem but during that time, her nurse, a man named david, became increasingly critical of her and our usage of 911 to get her to the hospital. why anyone would feel the need to criticize someone for this is beyond frustrating. my sister, laid out in a hospital bed, fighting the previously mentioned symptoms, was forced to defend herself and told david that he was being rude. again, why should someone in her position be forced to defend herself? my sister then overheard david talking poorly about her to another employee out in the hall, continuing to criticize her for using an ambulance to get to the hospital. there isn't any logic in his stance and if anything, it's just absolutely heartless. my family and i have been going to doctors hospital for decades and have never experienced anything like this. we hope something is done about nurse david so that people seeking help and treatment don't have to suffer criticism for doing so.

sadly had to use facility for an emergency with my mom- thankful they are allowing 1 person to be with patient- not one person at a time but the same person for that particular day. staff were professional and attentive. followed safe guidelines- they are testing all patients for covid unless patient states otherwise. clean facility- was quiet- room was a double room but most of time there my mom was in the room alone. free parking, mom said food was ok.

i have just had a second surgery in less than 2 months at sierra vista hospital with the greatest ob-gyn, dr angela halusic, and i couldn't have had a more positive, wonderful experience.  the hospital was clean and extremely careful bc of covid-19.  my nursing care was phenomenal!!
 i never waited more than 30 sec for a nurse to answer my call light and no more than maybe 3 mins for a nurse to show up in my room for assistance.  i want to give a special shout out to nurses shane, nicole and nurse assistant mary grace for their exceptional extraordinary care.  even my dinner was delicious and they even made great coffee.  if i could rate svh higher than 5 i would; they will now be my first choice of hospitals in the area.  thank you to every one there.
during these stressful times amid covid 19 the staff was amazingly professional, proactive and sensitive to the patients and their visitors.

review: sorry must give a review here.  my dad went in low some chest pain over easter weekend and they kept him there for 5 days pending angiogram.  five days later he had a stent placed in his artery.  the next morning he dropped dead. why were his leads not on him the next day? was he even being watched over?  i could not be there myself to advocate for him during the times of covid and visitation restrictions.  he called for help and who knows how long it took someone to come help him. when the leads were put back on him (again, why were they off?) he was in v tach. i'm hearing more and more that this "heart hospital" isn't as great as it used to be.  maybe the cardiac docs  are world class... i am not so sure about support staff.  my last conversation with my father was him telling me that drs and nurses were having a party as he lie in the recovery area post angiogram/pci.  my dad was my gold and unfortunately they robbed me of many years with him.  when i asked the dr what went wrong he told me it could be like 8 things... in my heart i feel like he should have been monitored more closely in the end.  if your loved ones is getting a pci/stent make sure they are highly monitored throughout! the report was that he did excellent, better than ever.  and then poof! gone!

i had such a great experience here today and was pretty concerned considering some of the other reviews. i did not experience anything negative. in fact from scheduling until the end was impressive. i was seen for my yearly mammogram.

note:  i was seen today, 3/25/2020, during the coronavirus epidemic.

scheduling, i was given very detailed instructions on where to park, signs to look for and where to register when i was in the hospital.

the day before i was called to see about rescheduling for after the pandemic. i shared that i would need to call and reschedule because i was losing my health insurance. she didn't hesitate and said no way, they'd still see me.

right now things may be different. in fact, before i entered i was asked the covid-19 questions, if i had traveled outside the country and if i was feeling ok, throat, cough etc.

i went to the registration desk and was seen very quickly by the individual that is the reason i'm writing my review, rita w. i won't put her last name for privacy purposes but lisa is your manager and i hope you get some big kudos! she was fantastic. so patient with me and compassionate. i shared that i was losing my insurance and she gave me financial forms in case i needed them. she was just great. i know she was really busy and took time with me answering my questions.  i would imagine being in a position right now, working in the health field, these workers are exhausted. she was so friendly and nice!!  

i then went and sat in the waiting area for my tech, sara. i wasn't waiting long, i went to the changing room and was in and out within 30 minutes. sara was great too!  very nice and i thanked her again for letting me come in today. 

needless to say, if i ever need anything done and a doctor refers me to chi, i won't hesitate!

literally went there with all the covid symptoms and felt horrible. i literally got no care and treatment and said their was nothing they could do. they sent me home and said that's all they could do anyway. later got sent a 600 dollar bill, the nurses are rude with attitude problems and the doctor was no help. i don't feel i got the service to even have to pay this bill. they need a major revamp because this is why people do not choose to go to the doctor.

i am completely baffled at how the va hospital in the bronx is handling their patients. esp during this covid-19 situation. the fact that the hospital thinks it's okay for a nurse to just walk into my dads room and plop his medication next to him and walk out without helping him open it nor watch and make sure he takes it without any issues is absurd. and not to mention when he asks for the tv remote she tells him i don't know anything and walks out. while im on the phone with him!!!!! 
the worst part is when i called the front desk to ask the nurse to go in and help him with his medicine and try to find the remote (because that's the only thing he can do right now considering he can't have visitors) i get hung up on when i say i'm calling to ask for assistance for my father richard reason. they heard his name and hung up. i couldn't even call and request them to have human decency to help my sick father in their hospital. mind blowing. and this isn't even the worst if it. there's always something going on here.

went to banner general on april 19th with severe abdominal pain. was reluctant to go during covid but it was so bad i knew i'd need to see someone.  all entrances were closed except the er, wirh respiratory cases physically separated in the waiting room.  no other guests allowed.  checked in quickly, triaged quickly, in an er room with pain meds quickly.  taken for ultrasound, explained everything.  then taken to ct scan, back to the er room and provided more meds for comfort.  moved to a room on 5, provided meds and allowed to rest.  diagnosed with acute pancreatitis, crazy painful.  after a couple of up and down days, started finally coming out of my own yesterday.  
all of nurses, aids, cleaning staff, doctors, respiratory therapists have been professional and very caring.

terrible reason for a review but definitely well deserved.  great job all around!

thanks for the amazing care, folks!

after experiencing the most traumatic and life-threatening experience of my life (next to childbirth) i come in to this hospital (code yellow) and didn't realize that my experience here would be almost as dramatic as the event itself. 
i don't use foul language and i don't typically call people names but i really don't have anything good to say about any of the people that were in their "helping me" ... and i can only think of mean names... 

i was crying almost to the point of hyperventilation almost the entire time... not one person tried to comfort me or assure me that everything would be ok(and in a real sense everything might not of been ok, and i completely understand that) or at the very least that everyone was working hard and doing their best. i was left in the dark about everything, my monitors were going off and they told me not in a kind way that if i could just calm down that's what i needed to do as they left the room. 

covid-19 has everyone walking into the situation alone and scared. and it is the most terrifying feeling to be so alone while you are experiencing the most trumatic experiences of your life and the guys around you are being jerks. 

i have no idea what their faces look like but hearing the people in the nurses station just laughing and carrying on and having conversations with three or more people while i'm scared to death and crying my eyes out alone in the room... waving for help for sometimes more than a few minutes...

i will save the person conducting the mri was the most informative and kind of all of them.

my 80 year grandmother was admitted yesterday into the emergency room with complaints of heart palpitations and elevated heart rate. no guests were allowed into the hospital due to covid-19. the health violation i am most concerned about is admitting a patient into a hospital bed that had someone else's blood soaked into the mattress. my grandmother got out of her bed and noticed blood soaked on the back of her shorts that was not of her own. she then pointed this out to the staff and after an exam confirmed that it was not her own, but that it was "from her iv line" where no blood could be seen to be the source. she had to remove the sheet with blood herself and put it on the floor. a nurse walks in and noticed that her fluid line had been dripping onto the floor with a huge puddle (also a health concern). also, how do you know the correct administered measurement of fluids if half of it ends up leaking? the sheet had someone else's blood on it, was wet and was on the on floor and the nurse proceeded to try and put it back onto to the bed. i am in shock of the hygienic practices being conducted in this hospital, especially during such a time of necessary cleanliness due to covid-19. no food or water was offered during her 8-10 hour stay. upon discharge, the nurse never offered a wheel chair and left her alone outside in the 100 degree heat without the arrival of her accompanied ride being present.
