this is a review for the hospital's bmt (bone marrow transplant) unit. the staff that actually provides the care has been excellent but the coordinators have been inept, delaying my husband's transplant by a week and a half because the coordinator forgot to tell my husband she had scheduled an appointment for a specialist who is available only occasionally. 
   the first thing he knew about it was when she began frantically calling to find out why he wasn't there. he said nobody had told him he had an appointment. there was a pause and then she got off the phone, saying she would call him back. she didn't call him back. instead, he got an email saying that his surgery had been pushed back. keep in mind that this surgery has been scheduled for three months and my husband and i have scheduled leave from our jobs for it. he has been self-quarantined for two weeks so that he wouldn't get sick before the surgery (his white blood cell count is very low).
   this comes on top of a series of other problems that started with both of us having to remind the coordinator that she had not sent us a three-month schedule--as we discovered when we missed an appointment early on. later, my husband went to the hospital for the injection he needed to take before they collected his stem cells, only to discover that the medication hadn't been delivered. 
   in this area, your other options are johns hopkins, the university of maryland, and u-va. we thought georgetown would be more convenient, but knowing what i know now, i might have preferred one of the other places.

the birthing center at sutter davis is an amazingly unique and special place to deliver a baby. i'm so thankful to have heard about this practice. despite having to drive to davis, i have no regrets about picking this spot for my prenatal care and delivery.

for the vast majority of pregnancies (non high risk), their midwife practice will definitely do the trick. i made a point to meet most of the midwives, and i really liked each of them. i was comfortable with any of them delivering our baby. they were easy to talk to you, thorough, and assuaged any concerns i had along the way. they and the broader care team were also very responsive online and on-call.

ultimately, jenn taylor delivered our baby, and amusingly she was one of the few midwives i had not met during the regular prenatal appointments. however, she was awesome, and i'm so glad she was on duty when we went into labor. the vast majority of the staff we met in the birthing center during our stay, too, were really thorough and warm. 

the birthing center itself is really great. they are conscientious about evidence-based practices. they care about the details, like dimming the lights. you can also labor or birth in a birthing tub (though, note during this current covid19 pandemic, they temporarily do not allow the birthing tub for delivery, though you can labor in the tub).

i enthusiastically recommend checking out the obstetrics and midwives practice here.

during this pandemic,  i could more than understand if the stress these professionals are under could cause them to be less than pleasant. i went down to the er as my doctor suggested because i had been exposed to someone who had corvid19, had a cough and was short of breath. i was pleased to see the very effective system they used to isolate and treat me. hospitals are scarce up here but i will always choose munson gaylond if i have the option.

review:
well, i guess spring break will become a do not leave the house practice in future years.
last year it was the hubster who after a gentle nudge from one of our 100 pound retrievers fell forward down the steps and broke his ankle on the second day of our camping excursion. (unfortunately misdiagnosed by an urgent care facility near walker, tx.)
this year it was my turn. i was backing down the steps to be more able to open the door wider to accommodate me and several items i had in my hands. well dang if i didn't miss a couple steps and felt myself falling backwards onto the concrete slab shared with our rv. i had time to say "oh no" before  a hard landing -not sure if i stuck my head first or my tailbone first but i had the wind knocked out of me (and since i haven't ever experienced that) i panicked thinking i was not going to start breathing again. i was unable to get up and thankfully some camping neighbors came over and after a few minutes were able to help me stand. by that time my son and daughter-in-law and hubby had arrived. my head was not bleeding but had quite a nice goose egg with colorful abrasions and  along with my tailbone (which i had fractured years ago),
and then a cut and abrasion on my elbow. i was convinced that it would be best to go get examined so agreed to go to an urgent care. sadly, the urgent care didn't have the capability to do skull  x-rays or a ct scan which the physician assistant felt was necessary to determine that i did not have any internal bleeding or swelling in my brain .
she called the emergency room at this local hospital and informed them i would be headed that way. the urgent care was really awesome, i could feel the compassion by the pa and she knew i did not want to go to the er but strongly encouraged me, so off we went.
of course this is when the coronavirus had started to manifest itself in texas so there were many precautions once we entered the emergency room waiting area.  upon our arrival we presented at the registration area-explained the situation and advised that the urgent care pa had called ahead. he advised that he just come on shift and didn't know anything about it. that was certainly understandable but he didn't offer to go and ask anyone either. took all my insurance and payment info and sent us out to sit in the waiting room.
don't get me wrong, i fully believe that people should be triaged and treated accordingly but i was surprised that we waited an hour to even go back to be examined in a pre-entrance room. the two nurses that assessed me decided they needed to apply a cervical collar-ugh. they did ask my head pain level which was a 10 at that time. they put me in a w/c and they brought me to my er room. we saw a nurse almost immediately who hooked me up to all the devices they like to apply to monitor you, asked me to rate my pain (still 10). she said i would be going for a ct scan shortly and then would see the doctor. it was evident they were quite busy-which they said had become routine there over the last couple of years. 3 hours later a very nice physician arrived and was dismayed that i had not had a ct scan yet. she advised that the collar could not be removed until after i had had the scan. she asked about my pain level which had subsided to about a 7 on its own. although i reported my other injuries they were so focused on my brain they never assessed them. obviously, the potential for brain injury was the most urgent but the injury to my tailbone was preventing me from walking without quite a bit of discomfort and my elbow wound turned into a burning pain whenever i accidentally touched it on anything-and the pain was not at the site of the abrasion. the md went out to the desk and put in a stat order for the ct.
an hour and 15 minutes later someone from the ct department came to get me. they took me for the ct and then back to my er room in 10 minutes time. 90 minutes later my doctor returned (after i had put my call light on and requested they find out if the c-collar could be removed yet) she removed the c-collar (yay!) and reported there was no evidence of any brain bleeding or swelling and that she would be discharging me.(double yay!)
the nurse came in to discuss discharge instructions by which time i was up dressed and ready to go. so back to the campgrounds we went.
i felt very bad that my son had sat with me all those hours, and was exposed to heaven knows what...with other er patients going up and down the hall to get to the bathroom with their gowns and masks on and coughing and hacking the whole way.  ok-i do realize that being a nurse makes me very annoyed when i feel like there are inappropriate delays in care of any kind. god knows if i had had a brain bleed what kind of condition i would've been in after 4+ hours of waiting for a scan. if you follow me at all you also know that i am a stickler about excellent customer service. in all honesty, i would not return here.

i owe the staff at mmc so much love and gratitude for taking care of me for my surgery last november. they all rock from my surgeon to my nursing team. love them all. even food service rocked.

thanks for taking care of me again!

i had a situation with my first child in-utero a few years back, and went to a speciality clinic at stanford where the pa (not a doc) recommended an aggressive set of treatment upon the birth of my child for an unproven diagnosis. when i asked if it made sense to pre-emptive plan to treat something that we didn't know existed/wasn't validated, she asked me if i was a doctor - seemed like a rude & insecure response for a very reasonable question. i went to a specialist at ucsf for a second opinion, and she correctly went with a wait and see approach, which was ultimately the right response.

additionally, i have found hygiene/common-sense to be sorely lacking at the hospital. i've messaged the hospital about some of these issues with no response, so sharing here:

- re: covid - you walk in to lucille packard hospital and are asked to use their anti-bac gel (manual, not automatic), they then ask you to replace your existing mask with a new mask. what does that entail? using your hands to retrieve your mask from a stack of masks also touched by hundreds of other people. additionally, the person scanning your temperature is literally in your face...an outstretched arm would help to increase distance between you and this other party. finally, the parking lot still requires folks to touch a button to get a ticket...really, hundreds of people, touching the same button to get a parking ticket? seems like something the eng school could solve in a day.
- er: took my daughter to the er at stanford a year ago for a bad cold/fever; reception had no idea who was in the waiting room or already checked in (they kept calling the names of patients who had already gone inside for treatment over and over again), the triage nurse attempted to use filthy equipment to check my daughter's temp, and the er doctor never even checked her ears. i ended up going to urgent care at pamf a day later, where my daughter was diagnosed with an ear infection.
- l&d/in-patient hygiene: get ready for nurses to not be able to figure out how dilated you are or even tell you they can't find certain body parts - kind of not ok when you're in labor and in l&d. also be prepared to be constantly disturbed by residents, vendors, lactation consultants even after providing guidance to the team that you do not want anyone other than your doctor and nurses to come into your room. on the hygiene front, i experienced a lack of consistent hygiene - nurses in l&d did not always change their gloves before touching patients or infants, once, a nurse was about to stick a dirty glove in my infant daughter's mouth after touching the ac unit! don't even get me started on the lack of hygiene on the adult side of the hospital - that's for another review.
- prescriptions: my daughter was prescribed an incorrect dose (higher than what was appropriate for her weight) of antibiotics for an ear infection by an ent specialist; i happened to catch the error after her first dose, but seriously, that is an unacceptable mistake.
- facilities: the new campus is gorgeous, but i was stuck in a parking elevator at the older lcph building a few years back. the elevator phone was non-existent and the alarm button was out of order. i was 8 months pregnant and had no phone reception at the b level in order to call my husband, luckily my parents were with me and we literally banged on a small pane of glass until a passerby happened to see us. they called maintenance and we were able to get out of the elevator after nearly 45 minutes of being stuck. their patient success folks sent me a basket, which included pork sausages amongst other items that are clearly not compatible with my religious / dietary preferences on my file; not a big deal, but if you're trying to make nice with a pregnant woman who was trapped in an elevator, seems like they could have thought through their conciliatory effort a bit.

review:
terrible & dangerous

it's freaking wuhan chinese virus testing, except they won't open because they're scared of rain. went on monday, they closed. went in today, closed, scared of rain. unacceptable. i need to get tested!

was tested for covid at their houston community college southeast campus drive thru center on june 8th, 2020. i have been trying to get in contact with ummc and called last week and was on hold for over two hours and no success in getting in contact with someone. left a voicemail with my information and still no call back. today is june 23, 2020 still no results. this is a hazardous to the public to be without results this long.

my 94-year old mom contracted covid-19 and bilateral pneumonia in a local nursing home. she entered the er alone and it was impossible to get info or updates on her status, because everyone else who had a loved one in the er was calling for info on their relative. 
exhausted, at 2am, dr. bustamante, gave us a thorough report in a kind and gentle manner. he gave us the ability to cope. he said the good news was she lived 94 years but her prognosis was poor. the next day physician's assistant cadiatou kept us up to date on my mom's condition, even calling at 3 am to tell us of her decline and keeping her word that she would give us a report when she went off duty at 7 am. did we want palliative care to make my mom more comfortable? yes! she was admitted but never got a room; the hospital was p-a-c-k-e-d with patients. 
my mother died without her family around her on 3/30/2020 at 12:43 pm, but she was not alone. the staff of mt. sinai cradled her as she left this life and entered a new one, and we are forever grateful. 
colleagues of these professionals are intubated and may not live because they got covid-19 taking care of their neighbors in queens. they are true heroes, professionals, angels. thank you mt. sinai.

my godmother's sister use to go to the cancer center for her treatment. she wanted me to write this review because of the wonderful staff and workers there. she chose to go to another center not at msq because she wanted a center that was segregated from covid. she also wanted a center that has the chemists within the center not on another floor or in another building. a lot of patients are hesitant to go to msq because all areas of the hospital, including the ambulatory center, were used to house covid patients. but the staff are heroes and wonderful and deserve the best treatment. thank you all

the doctor who saw me bluntly refused to test for covid, and also didn't wear a mask. i was left on a gurney behind a curtain for six hours and i was very literally ignored any time i tried to get the attention of someone passing by. i can appreciate that the er is a busy, difficult place, but this seemed like an astounding level of negligence.

a week after that experience, i managed to get proper care and proper diagnosis at mt sinai in manhattan. i was covid positive and kept for 48 hours.

but i'm not a dummy. i always follow up.

i went online in june to check my bill status, just to make sure everything was kosher. sure enough, the bill was still there. when i called to discuss this, the woman on the phone had no knowledge of the previous guarantee, there were no notes in my account, and i was expected to pay in full.

currently i am awaiting a "manager review" of the situation.

i went to mount sinai queens yesterday with excruciating chest pain. i was put in an area for people who are categorized as "not that bad." for starters, a nurse named maria prepared my i.v. on a dirty tray, used no gloves, and was reckless when taking the i.v. out of my arm. it was unprofessional and more importantly, dangerous. i'm getting a blood test in 4 weeks just because of her carelessness. moreover, a physician's assistant is the only person i spoke with. no doctor, no specialist, just an assistant. she gave me drug after drug in a very elementary trial-and-error way; something a kid with no training would've thought to do. my pain didn't decrease until she blasted me with codeine 5 hours into my visit. "if it still hurts tomorrow, just come back," said the physician's assistant. beyond that, some patients were allowed to walk around the facility with no masks; actual doctors did not attempt to facilitate a cleaner, safer environment. frightening experience.

nurses seemed friendly and helpful. always checking on my dad. i haven't seen the doctor yet due to limit of one visitor so my family is taking turns.

i was just traumatized at the memorial er hospital in southbend today.  i had been exposed to the coronavirus but was told my results would not be back for 7-10 days.  meanwhile, i got worse but then i got better, but then two days ago, i had taken a turn for the worse--fever, chills, cough, etc., all those symptoms came back with a vengeance. so, upon hearing that it could take up to 10 days for my results to come back, i looked at my sons and told them i couldn't wait any more. i had to go to the er. we called the cdc to see what we needed to do. they told me to call the er, so they could prepare for me. 

i called the memorial hospital er, and they told me to just go in and register. however, after self-quarantining for 8 days, i was not about to go into a public population and possibly expose anyone if i had the coronavirus. my brother called the hospital  and they gave him different instructions for me to follow, which was call them when i got to the er, and someone would come out to me. 

none of this protocol was followed once i arrived. i was told to just go in. yep. i refused to go in, so my brother called the hospital again, and the lady informed him that if someone is telling me to go in, then i should just go in. (all recorded by the way.)

now, i'm going to move directly to the er room with the doctor, and this is where i was completely traumatized, accused and made to feel like a criminal. (i'm a 56 year old professional--educator).

(i get it, and i'm okay with it.  he didn't  want me to breathe on him), but then he used his elbow to turn my head so it faced the door. then after he had listened to my lungs, he started asking why i came to his hospital to expose people if i had the coronavirus . (i forgot to mention that an iv had been put in my arm but not taped down because the nurse had forgotten the tape, and at this point,  i totally understood that they wanted to spend very little time in my room in case i'm positive--and i'm okay with it up until this point.)

i had mentioned the iv to the doctor when he first came into my room, and i even told him that the iv looked like it had twisted in my vein.  while this doctor was on a tirade, blaming me for being at the hospital and accusing me of spreading sickness to everyone, he reached across the left side of my bed and jerked, not pulled, the iv out of my right arm. he then left while i was bleeding in that room. 

i called my brother, crying and panicked, and my brother told me to take pictures of everything. because of my hysteria, i had only taken two pictures when a nurse came into the room, telling me to calm down. i showed her my bleeding arm and told her that i couldn't calm down informing and showing her what the doctor had done to me. while i was still upset and crying, my brother called the administration of the hospital and informed him how i was being treated. 30 minutes later, the doctor came back into my room to apologize because he said it had been years since he had done an iv, and he didn't know that when he pulled my iv out like he had done that i would bleed like i did.  he then proceeded to say everyone's nerves were on edge because of the coronavirus. i continued to let him try to explain why i he had treated me so horrible. 

when he finished, i then reminded him that i had complied with everything that i had been told to do while awaiting my test results and that i had come to the hospital because i was getting worse instead of getting better--only to have a doctor accuse, blame and make me feel like criminal--when all i was seeking was medical help.

a little background. i am 37, no children, actively trying to get pregnant, with fibroids, heavy painful periods, and seriously anemic. one frozen embryo left at the ivf clinic. i am capable of doing another retrieval but for now just the one. i have had a previous hysteroscopic myomectomy. mri was showing a degenerative fibroid approx 10cm. 

dr. milad is a high volume gynecological surgeon. until i was referred to him i had never heard this term before. basically he does gynecological surgeries and that is it... it is literally his specialty. where other doctors may do a few here and there this is his profession. 

we came up with a game plan all via teams, since we are mid pandemic. it was all great. i could see my images shared on my computer screen. his team was excellent at responding to questions or issues either via mychart email or with call backs.

the day after my mother was at the er sharp memorial hospital in which she was diagnosed with nothing close to covid19, she was discharged late that same evening and was ordered two prescriptions and instructions on her discharge papers. my mother lives in an assisted living senior home and, after i drove my mother returned there,  they called me the next day with issues over the doctors prescription for her which had excluded some of the instructions that he printed on the discharge notes. senior homes are very particular in which they require a "doctor's order" for everything to be very specific. they were telling me that they needed the specific instructions attached to one of the prescriptions. so i, called the er asking to speak with the doctor who she saw and/or his nurse. i spoke with two separate nurses and both were so rude to me. the first one gave me the run around with no answers or solutions and, after i hung up with her i had to call back because i immediately found out that what the first nurse told me would not work for the senior home requirements. so, when i called back the second time, i was hoping i could speak with the doctor and, instead, another nurse came on the line who was so rude! she would not even let me speak. she flat out said that "we will not speak with any family members". i tried to tell her that i was calling on behalf of my 84 year old mother who has dementia and that she lives in a senior home and there was a problem with the doctor's orders. she would not even let me speak! her tone was loud and rude and, she kept cutting me off and would not let me explain one thing. she continued to state that, "if there is a problem with her doctor's order, then she (my mother) will need to come back to the er and see the doctor again". seriously?? my 84 year old mother just had been at the er for over 8 hours last night, as she had to wait for a doctor or test results for the majority of the time and it was so difficult for her! and this woman is telling me that i have to bring her back to the hospital just to resolve problems with the doctor's orders?! i then asked to speak to a manager and she said (sarcastically) "well that isn't going to happen because today is a saturday and they are not here". as she continued to be rude to me, i asked her what her name was and she said "we are not allowed to give out names". i told her that when monday comes around, i will be calling the er manager and will be explaining the whole situation to a manager about her rudeness! she sarcastically said "well thank you!". i hung up the phone and i felt like crying. just because of this horrible covid-19 pandemic that is going on right now gives no-one the right to treat patients or their family members this way.

the nurses and doctors here are unprofessional and don't know how to communicate with their patients. i came here because i had nerve pain in my arms. they ended up taking me to the "hot zone" because my temperature was 99 degrees. they put me in a room where there was a window with 6 nurses looking at me like i was some kind of lab rat. they ignored all my questions i asked them about my arm and completely shifted the focus on whether or not i have corona virus. they drew 7 medium size glass tubes worth of blood and said it was for the test. one of the nurses was being rude and dismissive of my issues and concerns. i got upset so i demanded that they let me leave. while i was leaving i noticed 3 security guards following me. i asked them why are you following me out. one of them said we do that with every patient. i said you're lying that nurse called you guys on me. he said you were being loud and aggressive what do you expect. i said i don't want you following me. he yelled okay i'm not going to follow you can leave(while we were already near the exit). i'm never coming back here ever again

this review is for emory rehabilitation hospital @1441 clifton rd...worst experience ever! my family was lied to from the beginning about the services they would provide my dad. sold us on all the great things they will do in the 14 days he would be there. by the 7th or 8th day my dad hadn't made any progress. his case manager said he shouldn't have come to this facility given his condition and we have to take him home in 6 days. needless to say my family and i were livid. i felt like they just wanted any money his insurance would pay and didn't care if he didn't get the proper treatment they sold us own. to make matters worst they are suggesting to move him to a shabby nursing home or for us to take him home in the midst of this covid-19 crisis. this hold ordeal is just heartbreaking!

let me start off by saying that the ed staff and icu staff are amazing. the provider, nurses, techs, and the respiratory and imaging techs were wonderful in both departments. a special thank you to the nurse on the picc team who came to start my line. my issue is with the ortho/trauma/surg floor. i was admitted from the ed for shortness of breath. i understand during current times that providers need to be cautious. but this had been going on nearly 10 days now- absolutely no other symptoms. and i have a pulmonary history. i'd been watching my vitals and body very closely, my pcp didn't think i had covid (tested me anyway to be safe prior to this) and the ed dr didn't think it was covid. after i get up to the floor from emergency about 6:30, i am placed in a room where my vitals are taken and the nurse leaves. over the next nearly 7 hours that's where i sat where i got a quick "doing good?" a whole 2 times. keep in mind i'm here because i cant breathe. the attending eventually shows up and wants to test me for covid. when that came back negative she thought it might be anxiety. when i said i didn't have anxiety she pointed out they gave me an anxiety medication in icu. well you left me in respiratory distress for 7 hours then stuck me in a covid room after i said it wasn't covid so yes i was a little stressed. also had anyone bothered to check my bp (which was high when they first brought me up from the ed) more often, they would've seen it was still high when i got to icu. every time she spoke to me it was like she was speaking to an idiot. btw this woman did not bother to listen to my breath sounds until the last day i was there. had she bothered to be more thorough she might have discovered that im paramedic and that i understand how patient care is supposed to work. a cardiologist popped in for about 2 minutes. never saw him again. pulmonologist came in around midnight the morning i asked to be released. everyone just seemed to be going through the motions. they had me attached to a small portable monitor and i realized at one point that one of the electrodes had come off and no one had been in to fix it (someone is supposed to be monitoring this) so i pulled off 2 more- nothing. i guess no one is paying attention to the telemetry? i completely understand that a doctor can only do so much based on what they can see. and my tests weren't screaming anything alarming. but i told my attending over and over i felt like i could not breathe and i really didn't care for the nonchalant responses. i asked to go home. here we are today and i'm still having difficulty breathing, but now have a pleural effusion and decreasing 02 stats. i would really love to ask that doctor how many times anxiety has caused those symptoms. and still covid negative! y'all need to retrain on that floor.

my dad is positive for covid and in high risk group by age and preexisting conditions. he has been sick since march 12 and today march 30th he starting to get new symptoms and his cough got worth again. department of health indicated that he need to go to get tests done to make sure that there are no secondary infection.  dr martinez from woodland clinic called  indicating that er would expect my dad visit and they have all his health records and will take care of him. when dad  came to er they didn't want to do any blood work and told him  that he is "classic" covid case and needs to go back home.  after some push  they agreed to do the x-ray.  the issue is that with covid one cannot go to regular doctor for blood work or any concern and er doesn't want to see them until the is in total crisis and it might be too late to save a person. my dad is cancer surveyor and has weak immune system. getting new symptoms after being sick for over 2 weeks and feeling better is more than alarming and need to be evaluated with blood work and not by someone visual assessment.

the worst hospital in florida - no the country. the head nurse carlos was a horrible unfeeling macho jerk with a little man complex. stay away if you want to live. ive never written a review ever about anything, but this hospital is so bad i felt its my civic duty. during the corona virus they blocked anyone from coming in. i totally understand why. my husband was in there with a life threatening illness. when i called to find out how he was doing they made it clear i was an imposition. i ask you, if your loved one was in icu for 3 days and they never even told you, would you not be concerned.? horrible place. run as far away from there as you can.  i would give them no stars but its not an option.

i grew up here in houston and i have always known methodist hospital to have a stellar reputation, so i was very surprised at the extremely poor level of care that my stepfather received while he was there. when you come out of the hospital, you should be feeling better than you did when you went in.my stepfather was unbelievably worse after six days at methodist willowbrook. he went in with a uti and kidney issues. he was 89 years old, and before the uti, he was able to ride his stationary bike for 30 minutes a day and hold conversation with me although he suffered from dementia. after his time at methodist, he was unable to get out of bed, swallow his food or speak for himself. during that six days, our calls regarding his condition were never answered. because of covid-19, we were unable to go in ourselves to see how he was doing and with no communication from the hospital or the doctor, we were frantic. because of his dementia, he needed someone who could monitor his care and speak for him, but he was not allowed to even have a family member visit. we couldn't even find out who the doctor was that was supposedly caring for him!  finally, we were able to get through and speak with one of his nurses. she said that she would have to call back, but never did. when he was released, we received no paperwork or anything that detailed what happened while he was there for the six days. he was released to a rehab hospital, and then we finally were contacted about his condition, not by methodist hospital, but by concerned doctors at the rehab. only then were we able to get some details about his hospital visit, including his doctor's name. when we called this doctor, he was in absolutely no hurry to speak with us. we waited hours for a return call. long story short, every single thing about this experience was a huge disappointment. my stepfather passed away on friday and i am convinced it was because of the poor care he received at methodist hospital. i would give them zero stars because there was nothing about our experience with them that was good. i don't know how someone can go in for a uti, stay for six days and pass away a week later. shaking my head.......

i got to spend two nights here recently. luckily i wasn't the patient -- but i kept my man company after his surgery. i actually slept on two chairs bedside while he was there. 

i've been here before myself, but they seem to have upped their game. in addition to taking all the extra precautions for covid, every person we came in contact with was very professional and enjoyable to deal with -- from the cleaners on up to the doctors and nurses. there really was a great team effort. and it shows. 

each shift change, they came in and introduced the new people. they went over the necessary info and posted it each time on a board by the bed. each patient has a phone with the number to call to reach the attending nurse, the assistant and floor personnel. it's a very efficient system. and they are very informative to prepare the patient for what's going to happen and how to manage your pain. 

the food here was surprisingly way better than average for hospital food. every morning starting at 6:30 am you can call in your breakfast order from their menu. it takes about an hour or less to get your hot breakfast. you use your phone to call the kitchen extension. (hint: they're busy. don't hang up. just hold til they answer.) choices included various omelets, eggs, turkey sausage, potatoes, breads/cakes, fresh and canned fruits, juices, cereals, etc. the only thing they didn't have was toast! you also call in for your other meals at least an hour or so in advance. lunches, too, were good as well as dinners. there's a lot of variety and they try to accommodate all requests if possible. two standouts were their fresh sliced hot turkey with mashed potatoes and gravy and their mac n cheese.

the hospital offers free valet parking which is helpful as the lot fills up. 

the only downside was the day we came their computers were acting up so it  took longer to register and to be processed during pre-op. and a longer time than expected waiting for a room to be available. 

no one really wants to be in a hospital, but if you do need to be, this is one of the better options in town.

review:
took my infant to the er here after calling my pediatrician and describing her symptoms. she's had a fever for four days, lethargic, inconsolable crying, weak, distressed and in pain. she was having a hard time breathing normally and that's what i was most worried about. 

the receptionist was very friendly, took our information and we waited. the waiting room was nearly empty. due to covid 19 they only allowed one parent in w my daughter so my husband waited outside, even though there was a mom and a dad with their baby in the waiting room. 

they took us back to triage and left us waiting. finally a nurse practitioner came in, not friendly at all, almost annoyed that we were there, looked in my baby's ears and down her throat and said as she's walking out that they'll do a swab test her for flu, rsv and strep. she left and i hear her talking happily w another nurse right outside our door. would it kill her to be kind or friendly to us? oh well, i figured, not a big deal, i just want to take care of my baby. 

they take us to a room. 

shortly after that a nurse walks in and listens to my baby's heart. she said she needs to go see what tests need to be done and she leaves the room. 

we weren't waiting long when someone shows up to do a chest x ray. a chest x ray? the nurse practitioner had said nothing about that. i didn't even know they were going to get x rays. i wondered if they had heard something when they checked her a few minutes ago. of course my baby is freaking out the whole time. the guy is kind and we get it done. 

one hour goes by. two hours go by. my poor baby is restless and fussy. no one checked on us or told us what was going on. i walked out into the hall and asked the first person i saw what was taking so long. she said they were waiting for results from the swab test. i told her they hadn't done the swab test yet. she said oh they're probably waiting for the x ray results. 

another hour goes by and i called the nurse to the room and come to find out she thought another nurse had already swabbed my baby. after being there for three hours and hardly anyone else there we hadn't even taken the sample yet. 

another hour goes by and i walk out to the desk where the nurse is sitting there eating cookies. i told them we're leaving. my baby and i are both exhausted at this point and the whole thing has been a joke. another nurse snaps at me and tells me they have a skeleton staff and they don't even have a technician on staff.

i finally get the results of the swab test back and the nurse practitioner comes in and apologizes for everything taking so long and said there was a mix up with one nurse getting distracted and thinking someone else had already done the test. 

still heard nothing about the x rays, why they took them or what they showed. 

frustrating experience.

my sister spent almost 2 weeks at this medical facility earlier this month. she is a stage four lung cancer patient, her oncologist is in phoenix at mayo clinic. she was having great difficulty breathing so went to the nearest emergency room. during her stay it was almost impossible to get in contact with a doctor that was caring for her. considering the covid 19 virus and not being able to be there with her during doctors visits, i expected better contact from her medical staff. when she was released she was released on oxygen and with a drain tube coming from her side. we were given no instructions on how to care for the drain tube, there was nothing in her discharge paperwork. she also had a very large terrible area on her bottom that was open and bleeding that was not cared for while she was in the hospital. now that we have gotten her back to mayo and under good care we are finding out that the drain tube that was inserted at this facility was the incorrect one which caused issues and ultimately an infection that sent her back to the hospital.

a lot of these people at mclaren northern michigan lack the ability to take care of elderly people. leaving and elderly women with a low 70% oxygen and making her wait 5 hours is completely unacceptable. leaving an elderly man in the emergency waiting room for 6 hours also completely unacceptable then giving him a lasix and not giving him a bathroom break, so he pees all over himself on the ride home. i understand that we are under a pandemic, but not taking care of your patients is the most horrible and disgusting thing ever.

i dialed 911 from my home, and requested that my mom could be transfer to garfield; since her blood pressure is low, they told me she wasn't stable for transport; so the nearest hospital will have to do. the medics took her to greater el monte. 

emergency department: no visitor policy, given this pandemic situation. i would like to send my sincere thank you to the staff. pa anthony lim and np kelvin liu . no amount of thank you is enough during this time. your patience and ability to answer all my questions during this moment is more than anything i could ever ask for.

my 88-year-old mother presented to the er 5/8/20 for leg pain and weakness. at the time she was at full mental capacity, ambulatory with walker assistance.
she was admitted to the hospital with our concerns expressed to the hospital that we feared for her life and safety since we would not be able to be there with her due to covid 19 as there were several reported incidents of abuse and neglect during her january 2020 stay that occurred in front of family members and the condition that we found her in when we would leave and come back.
on 5/10/20 we found it very difficult to reach her, her phone was not answered in her room and it was difficult to get in touch with nurse's station. we expressed our concerns about this. by 5/11/20 she was totally incoherent and unable to answer her phone. at times an aid would answer and we heard her screaming in the background. when they held the phone to her she was unable to speak and she had no idea where she was. she believed she was home. the dr. (raza) told me on 5/11/20 that she was on hydrocodone for pain and when i expressed my concerns about her wellbeing he informed me that her bloodwork was good and she could be discharged 5/12/20. on 5/12/20 we were informed by nurses that she had not had any pain medication since she had been there other than 1 tramadol and she was diagnosed 5/12/20 with a uti and was beginning treatment. on 5/13/20 we were told it would be yet another day due to possible small area of pneumonia. we insisted on her discharge 5/14/20. upon picking her up she was brought out in light summer pajamas, a blanket no mask and turned over to us and we thought they had made a mistake and brought the wrong patient out. we did not even recognize what was sitting in that wheelchair. the nurse stated that what we were seeing were probably residual effects from the ativan that was given to her to "calm her down" why did she need to be calmed down and why was she given ativan? we were rushed along and given no real discharge instructions. upon getting her home she laid in fetal position for the first 3 days crying for her mother. she was covered in bruises showing all signs of severe abuse, trauma and suspected sexual abuse. at first the home nurses though that she may have been catheterized for the urine sample and that was painful and traumatizing for her but we later found out that they never even did a urinalysis and she never had a uti that they claimed she had and was treating her for. after a few days she began to come around a small amount and she could only cry and ask why they had done those things to her in the hospital and why they hurt her. we also found out that she had a 14mm kidney stone that was never addressed or told to us. my mother went from being of total sound mind and ambulatory (only experiencing some pain and weakness) on 5/8/20 to now being on end stage hospice care.
we have had several incidents with this hospital that have always fallen on deaf ears.  in researching the many websites, we have come across several similar heart wrenching stories from patients and families in this hospital and i am currently corresponding with a woman who saw my post about her father in law who is currently in that hospital suffering abuse and neglect. i have every intention of contacting medicare, state board of medicine, health dept. and any other agency that will shed light on what happened to my mother in that establishment.
i have worked in the medical profession myself for the past 20 years and have never witnessed anything like this hospital. i am contacting the large benefactors for the hospital, the press and anyone that will listen and help me to stop another human being from suffering this type of tragedy and abuse in this facility. i also will fight as hard as i can to get the license of dr. raza taken from him. i want whomever abuse, assaulted, and basically killed my mother held accountable.
**update since this was first written.
on june 9, 2020 exactly 27 days after she has suffered the abuse, assault, medical misdiagnosis and gross negligence my mother has passed away.
also, the man i mentioned that his family had contacted me due to similar complaints of neglect and abuse was scheduled to be released from that establishment 6/8/20 but had passed on 6/5/20.
i will fight until i take my last breath for my mother, this man and all who walk through the doors of olean general hospital that are unable to speak for themselves.  there has to be change, people have to be held accountable.
i have been in contact with the hospital and melody stuckey informed me that an investigation had been done (it took a day) and that they asked everyone on the third floor if anyone had done anything to my mother and they all stated "no". did administration actually expect someone to step up and admit that they abused, neglected, assaulted, drugged, misdiagnosed and wrongfully treated / medicated an 88 year old woman?  this hospital takes nothing seriously

review:
the emergency department here is very efficient.  with the covid19 things have changed. it is best to call the advice nurse before coming here. then once you arrive drive up to the tent and check in. remember don't park in the structure for emergencies. just follow the signs and head towards the back.

if you are not the patient you can not go in. zero visitors. most people just go home or wait in their cars. security guards walk around and keep everyone safe.

from check in to discharge it is about a 3 hour stay. blood tests usually take about 45mins to an hour for test results. if you can't join your love one inside you can just log into their kp account and stalk their results. the only results that don't post online are xrays, ekgs, ect.

our experience was pretty good here. everything is okay. 

p.s. remember to send your primary doctor a message if you ever come here to follow up. they will call you back quickly.

i agree with both reviews of janny k and tina k. i am giving one star for there were times, not many, that i could speak into my father's ear over the phone- briefly. my father passed away due to their negligence!! families need to be with their loved one's during recovering; 1 for advocacy and the other for support and love!! my father, prior to being transferred here from icu, was alert and fully cognizant.  he just needed long term recovery for he still required a ventilator and had a trach and g-tube. please keep in mind that this occurred during the covid-19 epidemic, therefore, visitation was not allowed. this was very difficult for us and the only updates that we could get were via telephone. as far as zoom/face time, the client advocate informed me that unfortunately we could only see my father 2x per week via zoom for only 10 to 15min. there was not enough man power to see your loved one daily.  this was not so pleasing to our ear but 2x was better then none. i unfortunately never got to see my father for our face time appointment; he passed away prior to the first scheduled zoom meeting. 
the first morning and afternoon of admittance, everything seemed normal as far as updates. however, the first alarming news was when i spoke to the case manager who stated that my father was not responding. my father was responding and following commands/nodding yes or no to questions prior to the transfer.  also, the case manager stated that he had an occupational therapy evaluation and that he was not following simple commands. this was also alarming, for prior to that day he was receiving physical therapy at icu and following commands. the day shift nurse that day did me the favor of placing me in my father's ear via telephone so that he can hear my voice. however, the night shift nurse stated that they were too busy. this particular nurse mentioned that he had 9 patients during his shift; 9 patients? how can one nurse be in charge of 9 patients? are patients being constantly moved and cleaned?  every time i would call to speak to someone, it seemed as though they were overwhelm or too busy. we received contradicting information as well. the following day, i inquired about the medication/antibiotics that my father was receiving and the day shift nurse stated that he was not receiving any- what? he had pneumonia- why was he not receiving the antibiotics that were administered to him? she stated that my father's white blood counts were okay and he was fighting a fever therefore he did not have an infection- what?? if your body has a fever, your body is fighting an infection! she informed me that my father was only being administered tylenol for the fever. i called the house supervisor immediately and asked to speak to the doctor in charge. the house supervisor seemed overwhelmed as well when i spoke to her. she indicated that if she had time, she would do her best to call the doctor and inform him. i never spoke with the doctor. i called the number that they provided and never heard from him. i called the night shift nurse that day and he stated that he was receiving antibiotics. i asked, " which one is it- either he is receiving or not"? what was there plan of care for my father?  the following day my father passed away. we live about 86 miles away from baldwin park, therefore when we arrived, my father was already deceased. the doctor was not present when we arrived and we demanded for him to come back and speak to us as to what occurred. the doctor did finally return and sat with my family and i, alongside with the head nurse and house supervisor. the  doctor used the term "supposedly" my father threw up and they stopped administering food to him. " supposedly"- what really occurred? the doctor looked at the staff nurse and supervisor when informing us of the incident-as though trying to make sure that they were on the same page. 
conclusion- my father did not receive the proper care that he needed here. he needed constant care for his vent settings as well as for his trach and g-tube. when we walked in to see my father's body, the staff kept to themselves as though scared to speak to us. as we walked the hallways, many of the patients looked as though they were already near death. i deeply regret sending my father here. the room in which my father was in, was not what we expected. there was no chart on the walls explaining who was the nurse, etc. the family pictures, that we asked the nurses to place on his wall, were not displayed. they were tucked away/shoved away in the closet. the room, although shared with two other patients, felt lonely. my brother mentioned as he was mourning my father's dead body that day( they only allowed two family members at a time), that a staff member walked in to ask," where are they taking his body." seriously- we just received the news that my father passed and you see us mourning his body- no empathy here ! please do not send your loved one here!

during covid-19, right after the travel ban, i was on quarantine for 14 days since i arrived from europe on vacation.  during that time, i fell ill and after a few days under virtual care, my doctor advised me to go to the er.  i chose memorial hermann sugar land thinking i would get good care.  i was totally wrong.

i was advised to go the the er by my doctor because i was coughing excessively, barely able to breath, experiencing pain in my back when breathing and coughing, wheezing and extreme shortness of breath even with using an inhaler.  my temp stayed below 100.4 so it wasn't considered a fever.

the er began to run tests:  chest x-rays, ct scan, urine-analysis, blood-work, i.v., etc.

i waited about 45 minutes for all the test results to return and during that time, i suffered and tried to breath over and over in spite of the difficulties i was experiencing.  finally, the er doctor returned (dr. b. parker) and said that my lungs were clear and that the covid-19 swab would not be sent to the lab because i'm not being admitted to the hospital.  i stated that i understood about the swab but i didn't understand what was going on with my breathing so i asked him again about my lungs.  dr. parker repeated that my lungs were "all clear" and that there was no sign of the virus in my lungs. 

i asked the doctor what was he diagnosing me as having. since we know there's no sign of covid-19 in my lungs, what is it then and what was he going to give me to help me breath.   dr. parker turned the paper around and it read, "cough - adult".  i asked, "so you're diagnosing me as having a cough?"  he replied yes.  i was dumbfounded.  i came to the er with a cough and shortness of breath and now the dr. was telling me that i had a cough.  wow!  

i asked him what was he going to do about helping me?  he stated that he was calling in prescriptions to my pharmacy to take but to act like i had covid-10 and still isolate.  he stated that he believed it was just an allergy infection and that these meds would clear it up.  i informed him that i don't typically suffer with allergies and that i had been taking zyrtec because the virtual doctor i spoke to recommended it but i wasn't getting any better.  he reemphasized again that the test would not be sent and that if i wanted a covid-19 test, i needed to go to another site.  i asked about an antibiotic to clear up the infection and he said the meds he prescribed would clear up the infection.  i later learned that the meds were regular over-the-counter stuff that i had already been using that wasn't effective:  tylenol, mucinex and claritin-d.

i believe dr. parker's only concern was covid-19 and not finding the real source of my problems.  i asked my discharge nurse again about my lungs being "all clear" and she said well they are not all clear and that they had a haze over them.  i asked what does a haze mean.  she informed me that the doctor believes the haze is possibly from a bacteria infection from allergies so he's prescribed some meds to help.  i again said i don't suffer with allergies but ok the pollen is high so i guess.

where do i begin.  this has taken place during the covid-19 lock down-no family, no visitors. i had to rely on the nursing staff to keep me abreast of my 85-year-old sisters condition. you can only hope that you and your loved one are never put in this hideous, stressful situation! although, my sister was walking when admitted, a few days later she could not walk and her speech didn't sound right, kind of slurred. (could not get out of bed). i requested a phone call from the doctor, but never got one.

i discovered that she was put on the covid-19 floor even though she did not have the virus. i was told that everyone goes to that unit until their test comes back negative twice. then they are moved to another floor.

the day after she was admitted i called her and there was an ear piercing alarm going off in her room. her door was shut and the call button was not within her reach. she was in tears because this noise was nonstop for who knows how long and it was ear deafening! she said it goes off in the middle of the night when she is sleeping and wakes her.  i immediately hung up and called the nurses station. when the nurse picked up her phone i told her the situation and she literally laughed! oh yes, she said, when you have an intravenous tube in your arm that alarm goes off if you bend your elbow. i was in disbelief! how could you subject an 85 year old to this who can't get out of bed and can't reach her call button and you have her door closed?

also, her phone was put in a place where she could not reach it when i called. this happened more than once! trying to get someone at the nurses desk/station to help with this situation was a horrendous experience!!! if they answer the phone they might transfer you to your loved ones nurse who might answer their phone, but might not.

 one day i called the nurses desk for the second time because i couldn't reach my sister, and the nurse that picked up could hear me fine until i asked to speak to my sisters nurse.  she then did the "hello? hello? hello? i can't hear you" act and then hung up on me.  her name is bethany on the third floor.  she could hear me fine! 

 two days later, after putting in 8 phone calls in over a half hour, i finally got my sisters nurse, who had to check first to see if she was his patient, although i was told later that he had seen her that morning. i told him what i had been through and how frustrated i was at that point so he than told me he would walk in there with his phone so i could talk to her, but once again the phone hung up before that happened. my 9th phone call, the operator told me she would connect me to the floor supervisor who assured me he would make sure that my sisters nurse would call me right back.

he called and told me he was with my sister but that he was having a hard time waking her. she would open her eyes but than close them immediately. he said "i don't know if this is her base line."
i couldn't believe my ears. no, i said this is not her baseline! he didn't know her baseline? he had not been informed when he came on shift of the condition of his patients? she is like you or i, very alert, talking and awake during the day. there's something wrong with her! i don't know how long she was in this state. 

turns out they thought she had a stroke! they hadn't even noticed! thank goodness i insisted the nurse go in and check on her! later the neurologist called who hadn't even examined my sister, this was on may 26th, and told me the report said she had fainted. when i questioned this, in a smart ass way her reply was "were you there? because the last time i checked relatives and visitors are not allowed in the hospital because of covid-19." (i wish i could remember her name.) yes, i was there, on the phone, and she did not faint! 

they claimed it was a sudden change, that she was awake and talking that morning. so i ask why did the nurse not know that comatose was not her baseline then.? it just doesn't add up.

my sister is still there and today she was not answering her phone again. when i called the nurses station for room 428 the nurse that picked up told me that "her board did not show that anyone was in that room". what????????? she has been in that room now for 2 days.  i hung up and called the hospital operator who assured me that my sister was in room 428 and asked if i would like to be connected with her nurses cell phone. thank goodness for the operators at fawcett memorial hospital. they were the only ones that were truly helpful. if it weren't for them i would have gone out of my mind!

we still haven't gotten to the bottom of what actually happened to my sister and we probably will never know. there's more, but i've already written a book! im praying my sister will be released from there tomorrow.

needless to say, we are done with fawcett memorial hospital!

i could not recommend this hospital enough. 
i gave birth here in mid april 2020...at the height of the covid crisis. needless to say, i was an anxious wreck the whole month before. i'd never been in hospital before and the one time i need to go, there's a once in a century pandemic happening. 
but i really shouldn't have worried because literally every single employee that i encountered at lenox hill is an angel. amazing at their jobs and with such nurturing and caring demeanor. i had incredible care from everyone here and now i fully understand that healthcare is a calling for these people...you couldn't do what they do day in and day out ...all of the stress that comes with it if it weren't. 
we couldn't leave our room because of covid but the nurses were so accommodating with everything we needed. l&d rooms are private and i recommend paying for a private room if you can swing it for after birth because i couldn't imagine having to share a room in the state i was in post birth. 
the only negative i will say....we did the hospital tour in jan or feb and i really didn't like the nurse who ran that session. she was a very straight shooter, no nonsense type. to the point where she was downright rude to some of the women who had questions. one of the women i felt so bad for...she asked a question and the nurse was sooooo condescending and made the woman look like an idiot who had asked such a stupid question. like i literally would have cried if it had of been me. it's like, i get that this nurse has delivered thousands of babies so she knows everything and it's no big deal for her but for us women, we've never done it and it's our bodies that will be going through it so it's obviously a scary time so it would be nice if the nurse running the session was a little fluffier and more considerate of the fact that we have very little idea of what to expect and want our minds reassured. to be honest, i was very turned off the hospital because of this nurse (i literally looked into other options because of that) so i do think they should definitely reconsider who runs this session because that nurse (think her name was lisa) was not at all representative of everyone we encountered when it was go time and is a poor "face" of the l&d/maternity department for lenox hill.

i would rather be paralyzed than go back to this hospital. when tomorrow's surgery got moved here, yesterday, i canceled it.

i had two major surgeries here in march.  i was in the hospital from wednesday through monday. i was supposed to stay until thursday, but i had multiple infected iv lines, wasn't fed, and didn't get meds, so i asked to leave a few days early.  my last day, i sat in feces until my husband came to take me from the hospital.  

just called the patient advocate to find out if they've improved. i would like to have surgery so i can walk again. i am an optimist and hoped they had changed their culture. after speaking with taschiya, i have less faith in lhh. i could be offered no assurance that my roommate would not have multiple guests who would not wear masks. that means i would be sitting in a room, possibly for days, breathing in random unmasked civilians' sars-cov-2. when i had surgeries with them, previously, they refused to enforce their own rules or the government's rules about covid-19. just an fyi, a lot of cases of covid-19 do not have fever or cough, but they are still contagious and spread has been documented from these people. according to lenox hill it's just fine for these people to breathing in my tiny room with me without a mask.

i previously held off writing a review or complaints because, i figured, i didn't see the staff on a good week.  if you have similar problems, skip the patient advocate, and go straight for the new york state department of health centralized hospital intake program and the joint commission's office of quality and patient safety.

well once again when i go to write a review i wish i had checked the reviews before coming to this dump. they should rename this place "let's not worry about what's in the patient's best interest. let's just go down the list of high-priced unnecessary procedures and check off as many as we possibly can in an effort to bilk the insurance company for every possible penny and if the patient dies he dies, we'll just put it down as a covid-19 intubation death medical center". every single quack that works there should be behind bars for being complicit in insurance fraud not to mention grossly in violation of the hippocratic oath. never again will i go anywhere without checking the reviews first. i'm surprised this cesspool even made it to two and a half stars!!! it is so painfully obvious that every single move they make is based on one thing and one thing alone - how much money they can bill you for.  we're screwed!!! this is the way people used to view auto mechanics but let me assure you this toilet is 1000 times worse than any mechanic i've ever been to and your health and your life is at stake. i'm in the middle of a condition (atrial flutter with tachycardia) that causes certain death if not treated in a timely fashion, but if i disagree or try to turn down any of the plethora of worthless and sometimes pernicious procedures they want to perform they just send me on my merry way. i ended up leaving because i would literally rather die than undergo what they're putting me through. big hospital makes big pharma look like child's play.

i have been to this hospital three times now in the past two years and it's high time i leave a review. my family and i have experienced nothing but incredible care and compassion from the angels that work at this hospital--from cleaning crew to doctors, everyone at this place is so wonderful and caring. when my dad had his heart attack a few years ago they were so loving and understanding throughout the whole process. last year, i broke my arm and i experienced the same level of care and professionalism from every single staff member i encountered. yesterday, i took my dad to the emergency room due to a back injury and because of the covid 19 situation i wasn't allowed to be with him throughout his visit, but the check-in staff and triage were so wonderful that i felt like i was leaving him in the hands of angels. i truly don't have the words to express how wonderful this hospital is. we are so lucky to have this center just a few minutes away.

had to go here for my monthly shot today..i debated as i m high risk as is my hubby with our immune systems..we went cause if i don't i can end up in er which is the one place i do not want to be now. the parking lot was so deserted we had our pick of parking spots.. at the entrance were a group of people asking questions, taking our temperature,handing out masks..we already had gloves and masks on ..we went in it was very deserted and kinda creepy..no one is allowed visitors now thus the empty hospital and parking lot.. the infusion room which is always packed had 2 people plus me.  the nurses had masks and gloves on..one of the nurses and i talked about how scarey this all is and how they need supplies..which is a shame in this country we were not prepared.. i have to stay 30 mins after my shots and i was never so happy to get out of there till next month ,which i dread.. a very different experience and attitude here than i have been used too for the past almost three years..very very scarey, sad, overwhelming..

dr. tong and lisa crouse were part of my son's care team while he was recently hospitalized, and it was very comforting during a very stressful time, to know they were kind to him. due to covid-19, i was not allowed to visit my son, so it helped me a lot to be in communication with the capable and caring medical staff at mad river community hospital. i was very impressed with their overall quality. thank you!

for the love of god, run away! under no circumstances should you take anyone you even remotely like to this place. if you have covid 19, they will let you die and refuse to provide even the most basic healthcare because "your life is not worth the risk of infecting a nurse". i wish i was making that up. i am not. and once they get their hands on your loved one, you can't take them anywhere else. they won't even let you see them. they go in and never come out and all you get are lies and excuses and being told you should just let your family member die since it isn't worth their effort. dr. wajid and huml care nothing for human life, you are just some disease to them.  the hospital is fighting hard to hide my reviews so you can't see them - they are trying to bury the truth.

i was not a fan of frankford but during this time that made all of that change. i took my father thursday around noon he had shortness of breath and a very hard time speaking. i could not move past the emergency doors for my own safety. at that point i was pissed off.  i'm not sure what i said to the nurses there but i sincerely apologize. my father was diagnosed with not only covid 19 but double pneumonia. let me tell you those nurses on the fourth floor west wing i believe took very good care of him! i thank you guys from the bottom of my heart! he identified a special nurse, kacy. all of you did a wonderful job. he is now home self quarantining. i'm sure i made the best decision of bringing him to you guys. you are the real hero's!

my father has been going to this hospital for a few years now and it is the worst! the medical staff is unfriendly, unhelpful and wait times are loooooong (both on phone and in person). our recent experience had us on hold for 20 minutes, 3 times and all three times the call dropped. when we finally got a nurse on the phone to get an update, the nurse didn't know and wasn't able to find anyone to provide us answers. they told us to call back at a certain time, we did and we're told to call back again.  father went in at 9 am and at 8 pm, we still don't have any information. i am extremely understanding of the fact that during covid-19 things are a lot different and more difficult on our health care workers, but this experience is the same as it has been in years. avoid at all costs, if possible.

the hubby had eye surgery yesterday. everyone at fsh was amazing. in spite of the current covid-19 scare, the staff there remained caring, compassionate and professional. they were taking precautions and everyone's health seriously and had a plan in place from arrival, through surgery, recovery and release. my hubby had the most amazing nurse attending to him and wished he could remember her name. he hopes to have her again when he goes back for surgery on the other eye. dr. fogg was amazing and even made a phone call himself to check on my hubby today. fsh called, too, to check in. although i wasn't allowed to stay and wait while my hubby was having the surgery, i was kept close by via phone. they called me when surgery was done and gave me instructions for pickup. i called when i got back over there and was given post op instructions by phone before they brought him out. five stars for every person involved in the care of my hubby and for keeping everyone's good health top of mind. highly recommend.

last night i spent five hours in this hospital trying to get treated for a horrific eye infection. for all five hours, they kept telling me they were four people in front of me while i watched 30 people go ahead of me. i do understand that it's covid times but i also understand that covid can pass through the eyeballs and i was terrified. well i respect others health conditions being greater than mine and would always put that before my own, it was very wrong of them to keep leaving me on and telling me that there were four patients ahead of me for five hours straight while i witnessed that being entirely false. after five hours of waiting in this purgatory, i demanded my medical records back, which they refused. i've done a little research and i don't wanna say too much but i'm pretty sure that's not legal. that's what my lawyers are saying too. especially since you didn't treat me! hour 5 in purgatory: i leave. on my way home, i am facetime in a dear friend and they witnessed me getting chased down by some random homeless guy and having to basically run for my life trip and fall and now i'm covered in bruises so thank you for that i'm blaming emory midtown for that too and posting this on my online stories. xo - g

the doctor, nurses and staff were so kind and empathetic! my daughter was running a fever and my husband and i had to make the difficult decision to take her to the er around 2am one day last week. we were so nervous, especially given the nature of the current pandemic. the staff thoroughly explained what their process was and assured us that there were no covid-19 paitients there. my baby was seen right away and we were in a room at the end of a hall, several beds away from other patients. the front desk staff were so understanding and communicated what was going on to my worried husband, as he waited outside of the hospital as instructed. our stay was short, all tests came back clear and our babygirl is doing great!

my mother was brought in via ambulance.  i understand the whole social distancing situation due to covid but an update would be nice.  waited in the parking lot over 4 hours and never got one phone call or any update on my mother.  very unhappy about the lack of communication to the families of those who are in there.  i'm literally still here in the parking lot and even after i went in to ask for an update haven't heard a damn thing.  i used to really like this emergency room.

went to kent last night do to unbearable stomach pain. was greeted at the front door by a very professional er tech and rn. i was triaged given an ekg and made it to an exam room within 15 minutes where i was immediately seen by a nurse and doctor. the rn started me on an iv and was seen then by the original dr and anther md who examined me. they ordered test and pain meds immediately and set up a surgical consult( the only thing i had to wait for) this took some time with all the changes do to covid-19 . when the surgeon came he also examined me and scheduled my surgery within a couple hours. without the great team that took care of me today i would still be in excruciating pain. thank you to all the doctors, nurses, techs and cna's doing their jobs in this trying time.

i took my husband to the er march 11, he had side pain.  the signage could be better . i drove up belle terre . there was masks at the door with  hand sanitizer.  they wiped down everything while we waited . there should of been a waiting area and a sick area   the admission nurse , he was great and caring . 
he was diagnosed with a kidney stone . no covid .

i had my baby here before corona virus back in february. i seriously had the best care ever. i had my first baby via c section and they were so doting towards me and made me feel so comfortable. from the wonderful nurses to doctor san ramos who delivered my baby i cannot thank them enough for their kindness and care thru what was the most important thing i have ever gone thru. doctor san ramos talked me thru everything and made me feel much more calm. they make you feel special with a nice couples dinner for you and your spouse. it felt more like a hotel than a hospital. they also have these delicious peanut butter cookies they leave out every night. the over night nurses went out of their way for us to make sure we were happy and comfortable. i can't wait to come back here to have my second baby and i mean that. i recommend this hospital to anyone having a baby! anything i needed they got for me. i went into labor 3 and a half weeks early didn't even have a hospital bag packed and they made sure i got anything i needed and i cannot thank these people (more like angels) enough.

wish 0 stars was an option. my father was in and out of 3 west for the last few months. he was a 9/11 first responder and as a result ended up with sarcoid of the liver and eventually a tbi due to a fall from encephalopathy. he was treated with nothing short of physical abuse with the exception of a few staff members such as one of the nps who was lovely and caring, when i called him, often the 1:1s wouldn't even pick up the phone, the nurses station only picked up about 60% of the time. getting in touch with him was almost impossible which was devastating since we couldn't visit due to covid 19. when i did speak to my father he would tell me they were abusing him. unfortunately, because of his recent brain surgery, tbi, and encephalopathy he couldn't come home and every time my mother inquired with the nurse they would always assure us he was confused. considering the circumstances and his mental status we trusted them.  a few times i called and i heard voices in the background being short with him. i spoke to one of them once asking to please treat him like they'd want their loved one treated. needless to say, he was put on hospice and transferred to an in patient facility where we could visit him. he was covered in bruises and had a broken toe and laceration on his foot. we were told he broke his toe from kicking and they glued the laceration. however, the laceration is not consistent with that story and was stitched inappropriately and sloppily, not glued. he also got pneumonia from aspirating while there and is dealing with that while on hospice. i'm disgusted with this hospital with the exception if maybe 2 or 3 individuals.

last monday i went to the glendale memorial hospital for drive-thru covid-19 testing. it was tremendous! incredible!! they could test millions and billions! haha!

in all seriousness my experience with drive-thru covid-19 was wonderful. exceeded my expectations. i signed up for an appointment via la county's website. when i arrived for my appointment, i was seen immediately with no long wait-time. staff was very friendly and professional. someone from the hospital even called me the next day to give me my results. i was expecting a 3-5 day turn around. i just want to say that the entire drive-thru covid-19 testing experience was very well run.

as a fyi, the nasal swab for covid-19 testing has a severe burning sensation, but what do you expect from having a cotton swab shoved up your nose to the middle of your head. besides the actual burning in my sinus feeling, everything about signup, testing and delivery of my results was great!
