review: i was very distressed to find they employ a nurse in springfield, mo recently back from mexico.  she was cleared to go back to work and did not self quarantine.  this woman works with oncology patients whose immune systems are already compromised.  isn't it bad enough they have cancer??? this should be made known to them so they may decide whether to continue treatment there or another facility. she's also, potentially exposing the other nurses and their families.  i realize mexico is not a high risk area at this time but she had to travel through at least 2 airports.....probably 3. if she stayed at a resort, there are other travelers who may have traveled from other countries she's came in contact with.   i'm so shocked the hospital has allowed her to return to work.  i'm so disgusted. the hospital is limiting visitors but allowing workers to do this!!

last january 2019, i checked into the er because my financial situation brought me to the brink of suicide.  i recovered after receiving treatment, somewhat.  i moved to henderson, nv in may of 2019 because it was a better opportunity financially.  having paid my $400 co-pay, i assumed i was done.  according to mission viejo medical associates, they sent 2 letters to me on june 5 & 10 of 2019 stating that i owed $1286.  since i had already moved, those letters never got to me, and i did not call, because i had no reason to believe i owed anything.

today, i checked my credit score, only to find out that they sent me to collections.  wtf?? they have ruined my credit score.  i lost my job in october, and had finally found one, only to have the offer taken away because of covid-19.  i am destitute, and i now cannot get a job in my profession because i have taken a huge hit on my credit report, and i need good credit because my industry requires it.  mission viejo medical associates has had my telephone number the entire time and never once attempted to call me about owing anything!!!   now they have ruined my credit, and my prospects for attaining employment.   there is no reason they could not have called my back then when i still had a job.  now my financial situation is worse than it was then.  and now those thoughts are quickly back in my mind.  mission hospital is there to save lives, yet they will probably cost me mine.

i have been going through a rough patch the past few months with really bad back pain. i had it under control most of the time but unfortunately it's with pain killers. it's a temporary thing but very much needed. i also have daily abdominal pain and discomfort from my past cancer surgeries that they already had be on the pain killers for. this back pain over shadows it. so they just have me take more for this. i recently moved and my new doctor wanted to try me on the pain meds he likes. unfortunately they didn't seem to take away any of the pain and it by the time i figured this out and told them i was already in very bad pain. then they took some time to respond due to the doctor being out. a little too long. this pain completely changes my life. i can't hardly get out of bed or do anything. i have my laptop in bed with me trying to work and it's rough. so i didn't know what else to do. especially with the covid situation. i wasn't sure. so i called the closest hospital to me, st. john's. they said come right down, they'd be happy to see me. it was a rough ride but at least they are very close to me. i got there and no one was in the waiting room. i thought this is great, get right in! so i got signed in, told them the whole story and went back to the waiting room. i then spent two hours curled up in pain on the floor of the waiting room before my pain doctor came through and they just put me back on the meds i was on before that were working. it was a rough ride but i got the prescription and took them and was back to life again. this was 4 hours after the time i arrived at the hospital.

it was a day or so after this that a friend of mine told me that they probably though i was an addict. this is the reason for this review. i am a clean cut professional, i can't even believe i could throw out that kind of vibe but he said that there are clever addicts that exhibit the same persona. all i can say, this is some of the worse pain i've ever experienced and i've had a lot with the gi issues from my past cancer. i was wondering why two different people came into the er after me and got right in. they just kept telling me all their beds are full. so i guess it's true. i will do all i can to avoid this place if i can. unfortunately it's the only hospital around me from what i'm seeing. but i am new to the area. i'll have to explore more and ask around.

i just hope they can read this review and hopefully help the next person that is in pain. stop thinking the worst of people. i hope everyday that most of us aren't bad. i know it's tough with all we see in the world today, but goodness does exist! it is a complete disappointment how i was treated (or not treated really). i am disguised with all of this! so sad!

the only response now is that they think i meant st jude's. i'm not sure where that is at but i live in camarillo and i went to the hospital right down the road from me, st john's pleasant valley hospital at 2309 antonio ave. this is the only one that came up by me since it shows kaiser permanente camarillo as closed currently. so this is why my review is posted here. what is going on over there? are you all okay? i even mention the name st john's in my review.

i had to visit recently during the c19 epidemic due to an unrelated issue. i came by ambulance at 4:30 in the morning. the nursing staff that helped deserve the star.

after getting blood tests and the covid test i was transferred to the covid watch floor till my results came back and care was good. 

my test came back in a day and i was negative, but still i was experiencing abdominal pain, and a high fever as well as vomiting and other issues. i was transferred to another area of the hospital where i was left mostly on my own, and i had to buzz the nurses to remind them when i need pain meds or when my iv was running out.

then a doctor came in to speak with me. i didn't catch his name, but he was an older indian man. he told me the covid was priority and i should be sent home. i was appalled. i could barely walk on my own, and still didn't know what was wrong. i started to cry and he left. apparently no one told him that i was waiting on being transferred to kaiser. 

i spent three more days at kaiser in panorama city, on antibiotics, fluids and potassium on iv. it took that long for my fever to stop and my body to start working again. when i arrived my kidneys were failing. 

if that doctor had his way and i was not insured, he would have sent me home to die. never going to hm again.

if i could give the emergency room zero stars, i absolutely would. whoever worked there last friday are the most unethical and despicable liars. my mother has some long-term illnesses and was admitted to the hospital last week and had to be in there by herself due to the coronavirus restrictions. they discharged her after treating her for adrenal insufficiency, hypomagnesemya, somnolence, and a bad kidney infection, and lastly while right side body pain. we knew about the body pain but not the infection or adrenal insufficiency, which they never called and told us after i specifically asked very politely to let us know as we were sitting in the parking lot. in dec 2019 i fell and fractured my pelvis in three places and my husband was not working at the time but we did have insurance then covid 19 hit we were not thinking we would ever be sent to collections at this horrible  time thank god my husband started working and making payments on my bill we were sent to collections less then six months after my stay in the hospital  i am shocked! we are insured and would never intentionally not pay our bill i on top of this had a horrible experience in the waiting room got a generic response from that complaint why bother if you don't listen to these complaints and do nothing! or have compassion!

i had a minor surgery at the center during covid and while i was nervous about surgery and exposure, they immediately made me feel comfortable and safe.  i had a great experience- kind and professional staff, beautiful and pristine facility, and great doctors.  i am now three weeks out from my surgery and am well & healing.  thank you for all the extra steps of protection, the compassionate care and great experience.

saw dr.soyoung park at this location for my lymphoma. she didn't do a pft test before giving me two round of chemo to make sure it would not cause my lungs problems. i had a pleural effusion and a trapped lung before the chemo so the fact that she skipped this is pretty bad medical practice. i drove four hours from kingman arizona to this place for my chemo and every time they would make me stay for three nights while covid-19 was going on instead of scheduling me on one day. this doctor actually thought i would put my health at risk to stay an extra night to talk with her and another night for a booster shot plus another night for labs and finally chemo the following day. not only did the cancer doctor not know about my cancer or explain how many cycles and treatments i would do but she placed me in stage 4 instead of stage 2 to try to give me more chemo then i needed. she only had a couple years of experience and didn't know how to talk with patients. there are good doctors here but she is not one of them and because of the experience i'm giving this place 1 star. i have found another place in las vegas with the comprehensive cancer center that is much better.

i'm writing this on behalf of my husband. dr. gage is a very nice doctor. i am only giving him 1 star because of his horrible staff. i am very disappointed with their customer service. i have been a office manager for private doctors offices for many years. so i have an idea of what good customer service should entail. upon scheduling my husband's evaluation, i called the morning of his appointment and requested that the new patient paperwork be emailed to us that way we could be prepared prior to our appointment. the receptionist answered like she was annoyed by me and was coughing into the phone as she answered and during the whole call. not sure why she was at work when i could barely understand her as she continued to cough heavily into the phone.. i asked her politely to email me the paperwork and she told me she couldn't do that with an attitude. i asked her why not, we do not want to sit in the waiting room if we could just bring it prior. she then told me i could look it up on the website if i really wanted the paperwork. i told her kindly that we were driving right now and asked her to email me the website.. which again she proceeded to tell me "well if you're driving you can't print it out.. so why should i email it to you?" seriously? it's takes less than a few minutes! obviously we weren't going to print it out in the car, we were on our way home from a different appointment. after minutes of going back-and-forth with her about why i wanted the paperwork in advance she finally sighed and agreed to do it. it took her forever to send the email and she still didn't send the link to the file! instead she sent me a bland email of what to type in the address bar and where on the page i couldn't find it. why not just email me the pdf or the link directly? or send me the link of the website so it could easily be accessed? my husband's evaluation went well and he really liked dr. gage. he was excited to go back to him for further testing. they submitted for a pre-auth for testing which then got approved. i then called and spoke to jessica and she told me that we would have to pay almost $900 out-of-pocket due to his deductible not being met. totally understandable! however, right now many of us (including myself) got laid off due to covid-19 and are suffering mentally and financially. instead of jessica giving us options like offering to pay with carecredit, making a payment plan option, or referring us to a place like terry reilly where i know they have a sliding fee scale... she just said she couldn't help us and "didn't know what to tell us about not having the money". she was quick to get off the phone like she didn't care about my husband's mental health. which to me is absurd because he tried to harm himself just a few weeks ago! you would think that these employees working at a behavioral health office would have more compassion for patients instead of being quick to turn them down over a high fee they're requesting upfront with no payment plan. you would think because of covid-19 they would be more understanding that people don't have $900 all up front. during a stressful and desperate time like this, you'd think they'd offer to give their patients some sort help or other options. before my dental office closed due to the pandemic, i was always helping my patients who couldn't afford my services find a way! i am so disappointed by the front desk staff that i will let my friends and family know not to ever come to this office. from the very beginning everyone there has been extremely rude and unprofessional. dr. gage, i would highly recommend interviewing some new front desk staff. preferably a staff who is more compassionate towards your patients going through a difficult time and suffering from mental illness.

i couldn't breath and that put me in a massive anxiety attach. i called 911 and the operator stayed on the phone with me.after that it all became a shitstorm.  never once did they give me oxygen. they didn't even check for my insurance.they didn't have masks on. they brought me two ativan and i told them ive been on it before and it doesn't work. next thing i know i had to sign papers and kicked me out.they discharged me and told me to go.i didn't drive so i had to walk home at 4:30am. its about 2-3 miles to home.no cab service was open.i told them and it didn't matter to them. its been bad there and its gotten worse.

my 73 year old dad was sent to the saint raphael's emergency room by his foot doctor to begin antibiotics due to a severe foot infection. the emergency room was very clean and quick. the receptionists and nurses in registration were very friendly and helpful. because of the current pandemic i had to send my dad off alone after registration. i brought him in around 4pm and he was treated in the hallway for 6 hours, finally getting into a bed at 10pm. he was put into a room with a raging alcoholic that they had tied to the bed. he was a constant nuisance. yelling all night and spoiling himself constantly. this is totally unacceptable. this person should've been placed away from someone dealing with having an amputation. instead he was left. my dad did not receive the care and attention he deserved. when i picked him up to finally come home he was exhausted and disgusted. he told me about the awful experience and he never ever wants to go back to that hospital!

review:
first time i went, i was dreading parking fee's, i've had a lot of those since i  quit using metro due to covid-19. i was happy to find one solid spot right in front of the hospital. a tight fit buy my parallel parking skills were on point. only to get off the valet guy watched me struggle parking, but he said "you did great, but you know the valet is free."  well thanks for that info!  

i got a quick temperature check, i was given a mask before entering to the check in desk. i was here for blood work, and the young man was super nice, quick, and gentle. i usually get poked several times.

second time i visited first surgical center was just days later, this past friday. i was having a outpatient tummy tuck. again the same procedure was done, then a young lady walked me over to the surgical office for check in. the rn's, anesthesiologist, doctor, and everyone who communicated with me at length was knowledgeable, pleasant, and sincere.

stay away from this hospital. they are not enforcing cdc guidelines and allow people to work there who refuse to even wear a mask during a global pandemic! this is fatally dangerous behavior, and they have completely unacceptable sanitation practices. the attached photo shows the two people who screamed in my face without masks who are standing in the only patient entrance/exit this morning after screaming at me from 18 inches away without masks and repeatedly refusing to back away.

i was told where to pick up my husband after his procedure since i couldn't come in (bc of the pandemic) and was told they're be out in 5 minutes. i was in the patient pick up area and the valet came over and told me to leave. i said i was waiting on my husband who had just been under full anesthesia and i was told to wait here. the armed officer came over and lied and said my husband was in another building. i said, no he's here and i am picking him up. she kept yelling without a mask on about how i needed to leave the pick up area. i again stated i'm picking up my husband from his procedure. i had only been there 1-2 minutes at this point.

the two people in the photo came up to my car  telling me to roll down the window. they removed their masks (and kept telling me to take off my mask) and screamed in my face to leave. i was waiting where the nurse told me to so she could bring out my husband from his procedure. they repeatedly refused to back away at all or put on masks, so i rolled up my window.  the valet started yelling obscenities loudly at me because i rolled up my window when they repeatedly refused to back away or put on a mask. i moved my car twice to places he was pointing at but they kept screaming anyway. the last time he screamed obscenities at me because he wanted me to move another foot. i don't know why they wanted me, the only person there picking up a patient, to leave.

my husband came out with the nurse. the valet and armed officer found it necessary to start yelling at my husband (who just came out of anesthesia) as the nurses were giving me discharge paperwork. i have never been at a medical facility where people are allowed to freely project their germs during a pandemic or scream obscenities at people trying to pick up patients...until today. 

truly disgusting behavior in normal times, and absolutely abhorrent lack of care during this time.

well this is the closest hospital to me and i've been going here forever. the hospital itself is filled with crazies and the wait time is wildddddddd. anyway i cut my finger real good so i had to make my way. of course this happened  during the corona virus madness.  i waited 8 hours to get stitched up.  point is, the wait was horrendous but zach who helped me in the er was so awesome.  he stitched my finger and it looks beautiful. thanks zach !!

i'm appalled at the (lack of) care my mother received at this hospital. the hospital decided to cut back staffing during the pandemic. the ratio of nurses to critical care patients was cut to 1 to 5 (it should be no more than 1 to 3). the nurses were so short-staffed that they often were unable to provide basic care to my mother, who often ended up dehydrated because they didn't have time to give her water (she was incapacitated and couldn't get out of bed), hungry because they forgot to feed her, and cold because they didn't come in and cover her up when she asked (her arms were covered in ivs and she couldn't do it herself). several times during her visit, my poor mother was crying and screaming in discomfort and pain, but the nurses wouldn't come for extended periods of time. we, the family, constantly had to call the nurses station to get help for her because they didn't have time to respond to her cries. she was there for days, and they didn't wash her face, brush her teeth, or give her other basic hygienic care. the nurses themselves told her they were operating with far too few nurses because of new hospital policy (a cost-saving measure). do not send your loved ones to this hospital. my mom ran from this place.

clean facility. caring cna's and nurses. i felt safe amidst the covid 19 pandemic. the staff from billing, front office, nurses and doctos have gone above abd beyong my expectations. thank you to nurse  karen and charmaine and cna's luisa and rosa for your taking good care of me.

yesterday i went to redmond urgent care, not good timing with covid-19 for sure. i was met by a wonderful system to greet and help patients with appropriate physical distancing including in the waiting rooms. it was relatively empty, which was ideal. the medical staff were warm, caring, professional and a pleasure. i highly recommend redmond urgent care for a great experience and excellent treatment.

- i'm not sure where to share my frustration but decided to start here.

having had a severe sore throat, cough and congestion for about a week, i went to my doctor (wearing a mask they gave me) yesterday.  i was told that i likely just had a severe sinus infection (non-contagious) but that i should probably consider being tested for covid 19.  they suggested that i go to the drive through testing at baptist east; so i did.

there was a quick drive through triage with two stops to determine that i "qualified" for testing.  then they instructed me to park my car, where i was called on my phone and told it was my turn for testing.  this all took no more than 10 minutes.  when i arrived at the first of two stops at the testing tent, i was asked for my insurance card and asked how much i wanted to put toward my $1400 deductible.  when i asked what the cost would be for the test, they told me that they did not know but that i would need to pay "something" toward my deductible for the emergency department visit.  emergency department visit!  you have to be kidding me!   those visits cost hundreds, if not thousands, of dollars and i was in a rickety tent in a parking lot trying to do my part to determine if i had exposed anyone to a terrible virus.   i got nowhere when asked why this was considered an emergency department visit instead of a minor medical or minute clinic visit.  i also told the payment staff that they should disclose the approximate cost at the very beginning of the testing process.  nonetheless, i put $50 on my credit card and proceeded to the second section of the tent to be tested for the common good.

two nurses swarmed me as i sat down in the testing section of the tent.  one took vitals while the other gave me a new set of sinus windows with five different swabs.  when i asked why so many, i was informed that they are testing for the flu, strep, covid 19 and one or two other tests.  five tests in all.  i told her that i had no idea they were going to do all those tests but she said that's what they are testing for at the current time.  and i am sure they are profiting for each and every separate test for each and every person being tested.  i went back to my car, a bit stunned from the encounter, and comforted my bleeding nostril with a tissue.

the covid-19 testing at baptist east took less that being in line at chic-fil-a and should definitely not be billed as an emergency department visit.  i feel that the hospital is taking advantage of the pandemic instead of doing its share to help those affected.  they should know better.  and they should be ashamed.
this hospital fired a dr. for wearing her own n95 mask during a pandemic to protect herself and patients.

university of pennsylvania hospital was fantastic in treating me for covid-19.  i was their twice, the first time to be seen for symptoms and testing of covid-19 and the second time for worsening symptoms.  the staff was friendly and caring, despite the craziness in the er.  the entire process from check-in to discharge was smooth and quick.  the doctors and nurses were terrific!  i would not hesitate in returning if necessary.
fac_name: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

review: funny how i go into pennsylvania hospital for surgery. lady asks me what i brought with me and i state phone, charger, pajamas, wallet, and a blanket. lady said did you have cash because if you do we will have to lock it up and i said no. now because of covid there are no visitors allowed in the hospital. i have my surgery and come home and my louis vuitton wallet is missing out of my bag. only staff handled my bag. they do an investigation and said there isn't a list in my chart with my belongings but i signed a consent saying i had no valuables. no, i said i had no cash on me. so the staff steals my $750 wallet and they tell me i'm sol. i'm beyond livid. so much for being one of the best health care systems.

review:
hospital administrators are about as smart as whitmer. set a policy but make exceptions to that policy whenever you like, but don't make that exception for everyone. so grandma gets to come and go in the maternity ward but grandpa can go sod off. 

also, during a time when everyone is supposed to be "social distancing" you can easily find 7 nurses sitting at one table about 18" apart with no masks, but that's ok since it's lunchtime. apparently you can't cross contaminate while eating, just doing everything else.

thank you to all the dedicated medical personnel and support staff for taking care of our community during covid-19!!! we appreciate and value your commitment and putting yourself in harms way for the rest of us!

this is a pretty top notch hospital.  i guess during the coronavirus crisis, not many people were at the hospital.  parking was pretty empty with no one to man the posts.  we came here while i was 3 cm. dilated.  since i wasn't in active labor, they checked me in and then had me walk around for an hour.  this was the most painful one hour walk that i've ever had.  i cried.  but all the nurses were really nice and supportive.  

after i started to become more dilated, i was checked in immediately and then they flew me down via wheelchair to my room, which was spectacular with an ocean view.  the anesthesiologist came in pretty fast to give me the epidural.  our dedicated nurse was super nice and helpful.  whenever i wanted some popsicle or some chicken soup, she brought it for me.  she was very informative too.  what a blessing to have a great nurse!

they were really efficient too, when i was in active labor, a herd of nurses came in to help out.  it was pretty awesome.  everyone knew what to do.  no one was super chatty, which was nice because i would have gotten annoyed.

the after care was awesome too.  the nurses again were all very helpful and kind.  the after care room was pretty spacious.  we really enjoyed the food offered at hoag. they gave us a celebratory dinner, which was so generous and thoughtful.  the food was very delicious.  we order the filet wrapped with bacon and had some cheesecake.  all in all, it was such a luxurious stay.  it was way better than the hospital that i delivered at for our first child.

hotel hoag is the best place to deliver. from the nursing staff to the service staff, customer service is top notch. i had an emergency c section 2 years ago with my son and was trying for a vbac with my daughter i just had 3 days ago. everyone was on board with the vbac and didn't make me feel pressured to do anything else. i ended up having a successful vbac with dr. illeck and it was the best redemption birth i could have asked for. giving birth during a global pandemic is scary and the whole experience was warm, inviting, and first class.

my 92 year old mother was taken to the hoag hospital emergency room by ambulance last week.  due to the covid 19 limitations, no one was allowed to accompany her, despite the fact she is hard of hearing and easily confused.  this is what two young women did to her because they had trouble with a blood draw and she had no one to advocate on her behalf.  she felt like she was being tortured for nearly an hour  she was terrified to be there without a family member to assist.  covid 19 or not, this type of treatment for elderly patients is completely unacceptable.  i do not recommend that anyone take elderly relatives to the hoag er until the policy changes.
these pictures were taken 4 days after the blood draw, so you can imagine what her arms looked like initially.
because of a virus that is less contagious and less deadly then the flu, i can't be with a loved one after bringing them in with appendicitis. please tell me how the hell this makes sense!?

i took my 9 yrd child to er due to a runny nose. during this covid-19 and one of the security officer's make a snark remark saying " this youngster is still here". this happened after i had stepped out to make a phone call. we had been in the waiting for a while, very common for an er waiting room. i didn't appreciate that remark.

i want to thank the doctors and nurses, as well as all staff members at hoag hospital for saving my 24 year old daughter's life several weeks ago.  we believe she had covid, was on a ventilator, in a medically induced coma and near death. the nurses and doctors worked tirelessly on her for a week and she came out of it good as new! they kept us updated during her stay,  which was vital especially since we are in another state and not able to be with her. thank you hoag staff, you have no idea how appreciative we are!

do not go to this hospital for anything, especially now during an pandemic.  my daughter went there for treatment related to her diabetes per our primary care doctor.  they incorrectly put her with people who were infected with the virus!?  they did not address the problem of her diabetes and gave her meds that the endocrinologist told her not to take.  the nurses were not washing their hands, and using contaminated gloves. general behavior of hospital staff was disorganized and unprofessional.  i literally had to sprayed her down with lysol to get her home.  she had to remove all clothing in the washroom and take a shower to decontaminate.  my family and i will never go back there.

five fantastic stars for pediatric 3rd floor!! 

my daughter was admitted here due to some issues she was having and you can only imagine how stressed, worried, and sad i was to have my 2 month old hospitalized.

the staff here from start to finish are friendly, knowledgeable, efficient, caring, and honest.
honorable mentions goes out to sabrina, cashmere, maryam, & wendy. you ladies made my stay as comfortable as possible & gave me that peace of mind i prayed for.

** an extra thank you goes out to nurse maryam & mary ann [audiology tech]. maryam took the time to give me pointers and educated me on newborn care. 
mary ann, thank you for going above and beyond for my child's hearing assessment. you are a rockstar in every way and i highly recommend you to anyone who is in need of audiology work. **

as a forewarning, the hospital has adopted a number of changes to their policies due to covid-19. temperatures are checked prior to entering the hospital & those will any kind of fever will be turned away. patients are limited to one person for support and in & out privileges are not allowed.

5/5 stars!! i couldn't have imagined better service. thank you for taking such great care of my child.

we had a high risk pregnancy because of a placenta previa. my week long stay before delivering via c-section was very comfortable despite the fact that i couldn't have visitors because of the corona virus. the nursing staff on the 4th floor we're so caring and helpful and every need was fully taken care of. the or team were so nice and they immediately make you feel safe and relaxed as much as possible. they talked about everything and anything to try and get my mind off of the surgery and were very nice. the entire surgery took about 35 minutes and i felt no discomfort the entire time. finally, because our baby was born at only 34 weeks, she had a nicu team ready. she's been in the nicu for a week now and we have nothing but praises to sing for our nursing team who has been responsible for her care. they are so kind, patient and forthcoming with her daily progress. they show extraordinary patience when they teach us how to interact with her and allow her to be her healthiest. we are so grateful for their support and knowledge in preparing our little girl for her life outside of the nicu. they are so calm yet precise whenever there's an issue, sometimes to the point that you don't even know something is not right because they are so capable of caring for her. if you are contemplating delivering here, know that you'll have no regrets as everything in our delivery has been above and beyond our expectations. we thank the hard work, dedication and compassion that each member of the staff here demonstrate, even in the face of this terrible virus outbreak. even the housekeeping and nutrition staff are friendly and have conversations with you to make you feel comfortable. it's really the best place to have a baby and i can't recommend it enough. thanks sharp mary birch
fac_name: Sharp Mary Birch Hospital for Women & Newborns

review: i absolutely loved birthing both my children at this hospital. the staff is amazing and provides quality care. i'm giving one star because of my anesthesiologists. i had my second c section, and as i was getting my spinal anesthesia the girl could not find the right spot, i feel like she was searching for a while, i even felt her prick a nerve or something because my leg radiated with pain. after a few attempts she finally "found it" while waiting for everything to numb my ob came in and did the test and i felt it. i told them i felt something and the anesthesiologists said, "give it five more minutes to kick in, i did a good job." so they started after 5, after they got my baby out i started to feel whatever they were doing- it caused me tremendous pain and the anesthesiologists had to put me to sleep to get me to stop moving my hands and head. meanwhile during the surgery i kid you not, she was behind me on her phone. my first experience with my anesthesiologists was great, they are suppose to sit by you and walk you through what's going on. this lady, i had to beg for her attention on what was going on, or what i felt. the next day i felt the effects of the anesthesia and had the awful migraine so i had to go back in and get a blood patch to treat it. i was terrified after the experience i had with her, but the doctor that did it, did an amazing job and the nurses- one named annie, was amazing. she let me hold her while they did the procedure even during this crazy time we are living in with covid  and i am so thankful for people like her.
fac_name: Sharp Mary Birch Hospital for Women & Newborns

review:
i was transferred here from the another campus' er because they thought i had the coronavirus and this is where they were sending covid-19 patients to consolidate them at one location.  i didn't think i had it - they just said my symptoms were likely to be covid-19 - i had one symptom, shortness of breath and valley fever scarred lungs - that combination apparently got me the golden ticket to get shipped on over to abrazo central campus.

i got there around 1pm, got one set of vitals, and was told by the nurse that they wouldn't come in, if you needed anything to call.  i talked to a doctor on the phone who said i probably didn't have covid-19 but they needed to wait for the results of the test.  so for several hours i was left alone until the night shift nurse came on (when i finally got a gown and a blanket).  she at least came in several times to check vitals during the night - got woken up in the middle of the night to get a second covid-19 test since they could not find the first one.  

the next day, surprise!, i don't have covid-19 and they are going to move me from the covid-19 section to another room.  i get a cardiologist who basically tells me i am ok to go home even though i am still having some shortness of breath @7am (also absolutely nothing had been done at this point since everyone was waiting for the results of that test).  they move me to another room on another floor @10am where the bathroom floor is always wet because the shower is leaking (where they give me toiletries finally - luckily i had someone drop off my phone charger, toothbrush and toothpaste, etc the day before so i didn't need anything).

i came into the emergency room today with my significant other and left with a bitter feeling of distastefulness recounting the interaction we had with the staff greeting you as you walked in.

you got that?! m-e-l-a-n-i-e! want me to repeat it?!" so rude!!! can't wait to get my father out of that hospital. never again

i then headed over to building four to the optometry department. the screening team there was also very welcoming and very professional. i went onto vision essentials and i was greeted right away by a very professional, helpful and friendly woman. she was so nice and helpful as was everyone else.

but they still keep their commitment to serve the and meet the well-being of the community- and they did an amazing job of it! i couldn't have expected anything more. this was definitely my best experience at kaiser ever and i have been a kaiser patient for 16 years.

this hospital is by far the worst i have ever been to.  i was admitted to the er early may as a 1st time diabetic experiencing diabetic ketoacidosis.  i was treated so unfairly and poorly by the staff in the er due to my ethnicity.  they made it seem like it was my fault that i did not know i had diabetes.  one of the nurses there named heather started questioning me about taking the covid-19 test.  heather explained i would have to take the test and test negative to be sent upstairs to a room in the icu non covid-19 area.  i was very reluctant on taking it especially because of all the things i had been hearing on the news and social media platforms.  at that particular time i felt that i did not need to take it because i was not experiencing any symptoms.  i also was working from home and had not been outside, nor around anyone because of what was going on.  while still suffering from my illness i was threatened by the head nurse.  he was a caucasian male named dustin.  dustin told me that if i did not take the covid-19 test he would send me upstairs to the icu with the covid-19 patients.  i took this as a threat against my life. i am already a new diabetic, my glucose levels were 4 times over the limit, which means my immune system was weak.  i was scared for my life.  keep in mind this is supposed to be a hospital where they are supposed to be trying to save lives.  i also could hear my nurse heather talking about me outside my room.  she was laughing and called me an angry black woman.   i felt so belittled.  if i were any other race other then african american would i have been treated better? if you ever have any other choice use another hospital!! this one has absolutely no communication. the doctor was out of the room more than he was with his patient than needed help from him. i don't have anything good to say about the ambulance or the living center next door to the hospital either. with those employees working at a place where the elderly spend the rest of their days you would think someone would've dropped down and started cpr!!

if you are a travel rn seeking an assignment in or around denver, co, i highly recommend avoiding this facility. i was recently a travel rn for parker adventist during the onset of the covid outbreak. right away the staff and the work environment were very off-putting. my "welcome" to the unit was anything but welcoming. the management and leadership were rude and didn't provide me any direction or answer any of my questions. i couldn't get the nurse manager to answer my emails or return my calls once in the few months that i was at the facility. a good portion of the nursing staff were cold and never offered assistance when a fellow teammate was struggling (i was in icu....you know we all need help in icu). on top of the nursing staff, the doctors were ignorant, impatient, and most had "god complexes". i was consistently ignored, talked over, and/or cut off when i had important information regarding my patients. not to mention, an anesthesiologist put his hands in my face for being "too slow" when drawing up the correct dosage of medication for my patient (it had only been maybe about 30 seconds at this point.....). lastly, what really got me frustrated was that i was told that i was going to be "let go" from my travel contract if i ever took another day off when i had to take a few days for strep throat and the passing of my grandfather. i am only talking like 2-3 days here in the six months that i was at the facility. after the way i was treated for taking a few days off for my mental and physical health, it was apparent to me that i was very expendable and just another warm body for this hospital to control. again, i highly recommend searching elsewhere. 

thanks for bearing with me. i just wanted to save my fellow travel rns and our patients from having to go through a similar experience at this facility. (:

my wife and i are being discharged today from the hospital after giving birth to our 4th child. we are upset because we would prefer to stay. who wants to stay in a hospital ? but because of the staff here , specifically the nursing staff treated us so well we don't want to leave. 

we were both worried about staying in a hospital during the covid pandemic , but the staff here has taking all the precautions needed to protect us and our new baby. 

this is our second tour at the hospital and we came back because we were treated so well. the nurses and drs are so knowledgeable about everything they do , have such attention to detail and have the best bed side manners they made us feel like family. by the time we left we were all on a first name basis. 

we are actually leaving our baby in nicu because of some complications  but we have zero worries. this will be the second child we have left under the care of the fabulous staff in nicu and have all the confidence in the world. i got to watch them on a daily basis perform such care and techniques and let me tell you they all work their butts off on ensuring our children our safe. 

so to all the nurses and dr.'s in labor and delivery, in post op, to the nicu staff
                                      thanks !!!!!!! you all are bad asses.

so i called methodist er to ask questions about testing for covid. the nurse i spoke to stated that even if i come in and be placed in the covid tents i may not get tested. the doctor will pick and choose who can get a test. so seeing how i have mild symptoms i may or may not have covid but i'm going to put myself in harms way because i'll be going into the tent with other possible positive covid victims and not get the test when the http://covid19.lacounty.gov website i went to to find sites states i can get a test no matter if i have symptoms or not but i'm subjected to possibly getting infected at methodist hospital and still not get tested by this facility.

my cousin was in the hospital fighting her 4th bout of cancer for 40 days here at arcadia methodist. of course this was right at time the virus for going wild. the nurses were as nice as a person could be that is over worked and over tired. thank you for kindness and care of my best friend in the world.

my father went to this hospital to have hernia surgery and ended up with aspirated pneumonia. we did everything over the phone because we weren't allowed to visit. we never complained because we wanted to keep the hospital staff safe. now my father is on a vent with ards. we were told today that, although he does not have covid, we could come and have 15 minutes apiece with him while he died. that was it. after that, they would kick us out even if we were wearing protective gear. if we wanted to see the body, we could go to their "viewing room". we would have understood if my father was a covid patient and would have done whatever we needed to keep the staff safe. however, clearly this is not about keeping anyone safe but only lowering liability. we were treated horribly and compassionately during a truly difficult time in our family. they didn't offer us hospice or pastoral care. they insisted that those 15 minutes was being "generous". do yourselves a favor and go somewhere else. make sure you call first so you know what those hospital policies are, but don't go here if your loved one might be at risk for dying. my father actually wanted me to bring him home instead of die there, and now i wish i would have listened.

my daughter was in this facility.  physical rehab, occupational therapy and speech therapy appeared to be very good. after a week it showed not much therapy was happening. 
 
the nurses ( most not all) lack empathy & caring skills.  not all seem to read charts or personal information. every shift has different ways to go about taking care of patients medication schedule.  a schedule is a schedule! 

my daughter was ignored having serious physical symptoms and i had to talk via facetime to the nurse since they were on pandemic lockdown.  i explained her symptoms that were a serious warning that something was seriously wrong!

after my being given a hard time by her nurse and being told "she knows her name and who the president is, "she's just fine"   well, she finally called the doctor on call. my daughter ended up in the hospital needing medical care immediately. 

if they would take the time to talk to the patients and get to know them, they would see something was very wrong!

the nurses lacked in the area comfort for my daughter.  like leaving the nurse call button, drinks,tv remote and bed controller within reach is important to those with physical limitations. most therapists get  it, the nurses do not.  

as for the nursing assistants, my daughter has some very thoughtful caring ones that she adores. they show patience ,brush her hair and tend to her needs, which can be a lot at times. then there are some that just don't want to be there and she feels like a burden when they walk in her room with a snarling face.

when my daughter was slipping out of her wheelchair, she had to have siri on her phone call me. not one person on that floor could hear her yelling for help! i had to call the reception desk! yes, she fell after the nurse arrived. pain meds took a bit after that.

i would not recommend this particular facility for rehab with patients that have memory issues and are unable to move their arms unless they are across from the nurses station!

after being home under my date my daughter made better progress.
fac_name: Encompass Health Rehabilitation Hospital of the Mid-Cities

review:
so disappointed. i came a few years ago and my son was seen by dr. jensen. he was amazing. 
now my new baby is sick and i drove over 45 minutes just to come here. i was seen by dr. jennifer lim. she seriously has no compassion or patience. she wouldn't even let me get out all of his symptoms before she cut me off. she said "ok sounds like everyone else in here".... like i don't care about everyone else!!!! she asks if he's been throwing up i said no. 
10 minutes later a nurse comes in with zofran to stop his nausea and vomiting. what?!??? i just told you he wasn't throwing up. 
i have not slept in over a week! i have been pounding my baby with medicine for a month (fever straight for 9 days) going through bottles of tylenol and motrin just this week alone. 
i ask her if it's something in my house because we're remodeling, she disregarded it. 
i told her my older son has asthma if this could be hereditary? she ignored me. 
he hasn't eaten in 36 hours now, asked if he should get an iv. she said no .. he's had diarrhea straight for over a week. 
my primary heard him 5 days ago, took his time, listened, and said he hears some wheezing in his chest. to keep an eye on it. 
the nurse heard wheezing. dr lim listens for 2 seconds and says nope don't hear anything that it's probably a virus. i asked if we could do xrays she said it's not necessary. i said i will not leave until xrays we're done. ).
stop rushing! realize that you may see this all the time. it as a mother seeing her child not sleep, eat, fever for days, at least act you care even though you clearly don't! 
.. they ended up taking xrays and my son had pneumonia in both lungs!!! 
i swear this woman was so inconsiderate and had absolutely no compassion!! i will never take my children here again! it's a children's hospital for gods sakes! we don't go to a regular hospital but we wants understanding people to take care of our babies! this was the worst experience ever. 
i left, went to little company of mary and he was admitted for a week. he is now doing much better no thanks to doctor lim
fac_name: MemorialCare Miller Children's & Women's Hospital Long Beach

review: during this time of emergency due to covid-19, i completely understand that the frontline is exhausted, overwhelmed, and frustrated.   i know this because i am on the frontline as a healthcare provider myself.  however, no matter what the situation presented to us, we are to be empathetic, compassionate and respectful to each patient that we treat.  i did not experience this from dr. mendoza or stacy, np (sp) during an e.r. visit with my daughter on march 22, 2020.  stacy was very dismissive, argumentative and continued to minimize my daughter's condition.  no matter what my daughter told her, the bottom line is that stacy was not actively listening.  because this was the second time within two days that my daughter had presented to the emergency room with these symptoms, this was an urgent situation for us.  who would go into an emergency room where there is a greater chance to be exposed to corona if it wasn't an emergency? in my experience, a patient knows their body and how they feel and we as healthcare workers should listen and not dismiss what they are saying.  we are not always right and don't have the right to tell a patient how they feel.  stacy comes in to discharge my daughter after barely assessing her a few hours before.  there was no end result except to go home.  no.  the problem has not been resolved.  the reason why we are back here a second time is because of the dismissive attitude  presented before.  apparently there is something seriously wrong.  i asked to speak to the charge nurse but somehow dr. mendoza, who never treated my daughter at all, found her way into the room.  she, just like stacy, refused to listen to our concerns and basically in a nutshell told us that they would not be doing anything for my daughter and for her to go home and 'stick it out'.  for hippa related issues, i won't go into detail my daughter's condition but it involves constant vomiting, diarrhea and severe stomach pain.  she cannot even keep down water.  severe dehydration is an overwhelming threat at this point.  dehydration leads to other medical conditions like heart problems or kidney failure.  because i have a healthcare background and know that there is a standard that should be met when taking care of people, my mind is completely blown by the behaviors of these two healthcare providers.  again, i understand the stress that we are all under but at the end of it all, when you are present with a patient, be present and actually be of help and not hinder an already stressful situation.  i have had pretty good experiences at south sub before so i am extremely disappointed and will be requesting that if myself or any family member is in the e.r. again, that these two not be in charge of our care.  they need sensitivity and active listening training asap.  if something worsens with my daughter's condition because of their insensitivity and dismissals, there will be legal action taken.

with the scare of covid19, i called the covid hotline and explained my symptoms to the nurse on the phones. she instructed me to go on to the er to be seen and possibly tested. i went to this hospital because they did amazing when my mom was transferred there after having 3 heart attacks. 
when i got there, everyone was confused and a little irritated that they didn't know what all was going on. this didn't bother me at all because i know it's a very scary time to be a nurse or dr right now. this covid19 is new and the rules keep changing. i appreciated everyone's demeanor and positivity. everyone. from the ladies at the screening desk, to the triage nurse, all the way back to the nurses elise and anne (i think were their names). i got taken back to a special area where they were screening for covid19. it was a little scary because they were wearing plastic robes over their clothes... 
elise was the nurse that took care of me and she was so amazing. super sweet, and did a good job of keeping my mind off feeling miserable. these doctors and nurses are working their butts off. i mean, elise had to write my info down on a paper towel bc they didn't have all the supplies that needed. everyone i saw was working double time, and staying positive for the patients. i could over hear conversations from my virtual bed, and they don't have it easy at all. please keep this in mind when you see a a nurse or doctor and they look worn out. they've for sure earned a gold medal during this time. i wasn't able to be tested bc i didn't meet criteria. but i still have to quarantine for 14 days. thank you, seton, for trying your best to stay ahead of this virus going around.

my father was recently a frequent patient here as he neared the end of his life with several health complications.  the entire staff was incredibly kind, caring, sensitive, and patient focused.  ellen in the er was especially great.  no emergency room/hospital visit is a good thing but the good people here make it as pleasant as it can possibly be.  i hope and pray for all the good people here to help get us through this covid19 mess.

i was admitted to ascension seton on 38th street on wednesday, june 10, 2020, with an infection which triggered a multiple sclerosis flare up.  i am on the 5th floor, being cared for by the nurses and clinical assistants from the 5th floor nurses' station south.  they are amazing. even in these dangerous times, with half the hallway reserved for covid19 patients, nurses and clinical assistants have shown me unparalleled amounts of compassion, kindness, understanding and concern.  even at end of shift, their attitude, never changes.  they remain patient, kind, caring. these nurses and clinical assistants are true heroes, flesh and blood angels. i pray that god showers each and every one of them and their loved ones with an abundance of blessings, good fortune, excellent health and a long life. i pray that god looks after each of them and their loved ones and keeps them safe. i wish i could do more to express my gratitude and appreciation.  i am humbled by their grace and generosity.

i hope you don't have to recover at this hospital after a major surgery!!!

the surgeon and physical therapist were fine. the one star is for the doctor overseeing her case and the nursing staff. my sister had a complete knee replacement, and due to covid, i was not allowed to visit her and be her advocate. 

she was not given her pain meds at the correct times so she would be in excruciating pain with no relief. she was never able to stay ahead of the pain. she was made to feel like a drug addict for asking for the pain meds she was allowed to have. one nurse was not even able to help my sister test her blood sugar because she could not manage to get the blood strip to my sister's finger.

the doctor did not seem to understand anything about my sister's type one diabetes and how to deal with her high blood sugar. the doctor also misread the chart and told the nurse to give my sister potassium. her potassium levels were fine, she was wrongly given potassium when she did not need it. 

i'm not sure if it's incompetence, not enough staff, or just laziness- most likely all of the above.

this is the worst hospital ever for medical bills! they owed my daughter over $300 for three months. thank goodness for the time off because she's had time to talk on the phone or hold on the phone for hours and hours. do you not give you them your money until you know you owe it to them. if she owed them money of this sorts they would send bill collectors out for her. this all started to before the virus and it is a matter of money not the hospital. thank you to all the front line workers! the billing department should be ashamed of themselves or get someone in there that doesn't lie!!! sad

i was very disturbed when i saw on the news this morning firemen and pd with their vehicles lined up, lights flashing waving and honoring the nurses for their fantastic job and dedication and hard work during this pandemic. now my explanation why this disturbed me so much!  my 88 yr old mother was a patient at o'connor's in may 2018. she had a serious case of sepsis. she has advanced alzheimer's and was unable to talk, feed herself so i stayed with her. she was on a continous iv of strong antibiotics for 8 days. the antibiotics tend to give a person diarrhea. i was there to feed her and be her voice. one day she had diarrhea very bad, i could hear it. i rang the bell for the nurse, 5 or so minutes she came. i said it is real bad i could hear it. she said well i have to find help. 10 minutes later i went searching for her, she was with someone else. i said my mom beeds changed now, it's been about 15 minutes. she said i'm still looking. she finally comes in with an aid about 10 minutes later. it was a mess. the aud did not even clean her well because the nurse told her to wipe her again. this was on the 5th floor. then twice they did not do the iv correctly. i reached over to pull my mom's blanket up and it was wet, her gown was soaked, the sheets were soaked. the nurse came in and changed it, then they changed the bed and her gown. well low and behold about an hour later her arm was wet again. they had to redo it. finally my mom was ready to be released. at home when i went to change her had a rash all over her but, between her legs and all over her thighs from their lack of proper care for my mom. if i would have seen it, i would have been arrested for smacking the shit out of all of the useless, uncaring worthless nurses. this was on floor 5. i called and complained and sent pictures of my mom. i was unable to go in person and complain since i was sole caretaker for her. but they got the pictures the day after she was released.
this did not happen during a pandemic when the nurses were streched to their limit. it was just plain negligence on their part. and now they being admired as godly. all they are doing is their jobs, which they should have done when my mom was their patient!  so yes i was irritated to see
the news this morning. i for one hope o'connor nurses one day you experience the same care you put my mom through!

having a severe tonsil infection is scary enough without it being in the middle of the covid 19 crisis. dr.rostom can be intimidating at times with how strait forward she is because she cares very much for her patients. she always made sure i understood what was happening, what the treatment plan was and the risks of what could happen. she did everything in her power to keep me from ending up in the hospital including reducing my risk of further infection by seeing me daily before office hours. i highly recommend her!!

called to see if i needed to call ahead before going into the er especially with covid-19 being taken very seriously. i just wanted to know if i had to call in advance before showing up. i don't work there, so obviously i don't know if they are doing anything different to keep everyone safe. my husband was in severe pain and his face was swelling from a tooth infection. i was already nervous and instead of making me feel at ease, the woman who helped me (lucy) on the phone was very rude. there was no empathy in her tone and it seemed as if she did not care. she even laughed when i expressed my concerns about going into the er. i have never had anyone in the medical field make me feel the way she did.

two weeks ago my mom was on a ventilator and struggling to survive.  she was sick with covid-19 and had pneumonia and the prognosis was not good.  the situation was grim and i honestly didn't think i'd ever be able to speak to her again.  there was nothing i could do to help but emanate hospital helped her and they saved her life. she was on a ventilator for almost three weeks and they worked hard to keep her alive.  it's not much, but i felt that at the bare minimum i could write this and hope that their ccu doctors and nurses see this someday so they can get a small glimpse of how truly grateful i am.

last week i went for a mamogram and had a very satisfying experience. the staff were very polite all the way from the registration office to the radiology office.the hospital was very clean and the covid protocols were followed. i was hesitant to leave my house in these scary times but i was surprised to see a high level of diligence and effort that was put in making patients feel safe so that we could take care of our annual check-ups. thanks emanate for putting patient safety first.

ok, nice enough staff, but didn't receive insurance estimates ahead of procedure. my dr provided a brief explanation of the results while i was still groggy and coming out of sedation. when i asked my discharge nurse if dr. would be following up, i was curtly told the dr. has already explained my results. also, when i scheduled my appointment, i was told i would be receiving out of pocket estimates in advance of my appointment but was not sent anything. due to covid, the office was not answering the phones and the outgoing message instructed leaving messages for urgent requests only. i called my insurance to confirm coverage only to come in to my appointment and be presented with a very high facility charge (plus potential for other charges). i was of course very upset and questioned why i wasn't provided this earlier and was told sarcastically by the person at the front desk that she "knew this could all be very confusing" and she didn't send this info earlier because covid meant she "didn't have the time".  if i didn't need this procedure, i would have cancelled.

this hospital has been the best for my family. my dad is recovering from covid-19  and they have been really thoughtful in keeping us updated on his progress. they have even let us facetime him. debbie cochran lets us visit via facetime every morning. she takes time out of her busy schedule so that we can see him. i believe that she is a big part of his recovery. thank you debbie ! your are the most wonderful person .

my mom's been in there for rehabilitation since valley hospital. every time i call the nurses they are busy and minister and medicines two hour wait never call you back even when you leave your name and number. i know the coronavirus is going around but i'm gonna tell you something that should be in one immediate family allowed to go visit people in there because the standard of care i don't really think it's that great especially when they know family's not around because of this this is even worse i think i'm gonna go against medical consent be pulling her out. asked to speak to the doctor and have them call me for days ago obviously there's no doctor that works in that hospital bed yet i might even call the medical board and put a complaint in. well ask him to sign consents forms for my mom because i'm the poa and they wanted the other nurse to do it i'm like no i don't know what she signing people are ridiculous so help me god if something happens to my mother.
it's 4/11 and i asked for my mom could be showered because we're not allowed to go in because of the covid-19 she's been in there one month and they told me they need an order from the doctor. it used to be a cna and everybody got to shower every other day and washed up and in between that and where is this coming from that you don't shower people now without a doctors approval.

the corona virus came. my husband, who has dementia, was unable to go the the cleveland clinic for his pt , nor to the anthem gym, and began a downward spiral. a month into quarantine, he suffered a heart attack and had a stint placed into his left artery. after his week stay at st rose siena, he was sent to kindred to rehabilitate. they promised i'd be able to communicate with him weekly via facetime, that they'd communicate his status daily, and that i'd be able to speak to him daily. well, that never happened . after 2 weeks of struggling to get folks to call me back, to set up a facetime chat, i drove to the facility and had to demand to see him, at least through a window. when i finally was assisted, i found  that he was not improving. the staff had no idea how to help get him to stand or get out of bed.but worst of all, they never shaved him. he had quite a beard which i know he hates. then , they gave up and said they were going to have to discharge him. quite frustrating. one would think the staff would be more humane during these times loved ones can't get into care facilities. if your loved one has special needs, stay away from kindred.

a family member had to stay at acuity's long term acute care hospital and we had a horrible experience. we had done research online prior to the admission and we learned that ltac hospitals in general provide poor quality of care. we hoped this place would be different but unfortunately, this place proved us wrong. 

some of the individual nurses and staff we managed to talk to were nice but overall, the administration and attitudes of most of the staff were unhelpful and uncaring. due to covid-19, family couldn't visit so it was very difficult to keep in touch with our family member. we were told that staff were stepping up to help keep us in touch but it was like pulling teeth. they acted like we were crazy because we wanted to keep in touch with our family. we would have to leave multiple messages just to get any response.
fac_name: Acuity Specialty Hospital - Southern New Jersey

review: admitted through er for possible corona virus .  disgusting hospital room. paint chipped walls , filthy  bathroom and food trays piled up ..employees do as little as possible . worse hospital i have ever been in .
fac_name: Tulane University Hospital & Clinic Partners Prgrm

review:
#1 son had swelling on his face and feeling lethargic and urgent care saw something suspicious on his chest x-ray so they sent us here to the ermmediately. 

this is my first experience with this hospital, it is closest to our new retirement town and it takes approximately 20-25 minutes by car to get here unless of course the seasonal traffic is heavy. that's a big change for me since,  in all the 12 states that i have lived in, i have always been pretty close to an er. but it is what it is. 

the covid protocols are very strictly enforced here, there's a person asking questions and taking temperatures outside and they give you a mask if you don't have one. they only allow adult patients to enter however i am my son's medical proxy so i accompanied him for the whole process. 

the wait didn't look bad at all however the urgent care called ahead and we were taken right away. i worked in er's for several years both in the navy and in a civilian trauma center so my critique will be from an insiders prospective.

the receptionists demeanor, efficient and professionalism was very good. we made it through the paperwork and were taken back very quickly. once inside there was a triage nurse who whisked us into an exam bay, two other nurses quickly hooked matt up to a monitor and got his vitals while putting in an iv line. they drew blood from the iv, which proved to later be a problem, and the portable x-ray was done within minutes. 

a phlebotomist arrived in approximately ten minutes to draw five new tubes of blood commenting that the nurses needed to get up to speed on their, apparently new, iv setups as the original draws had hemolized. that's an unfortunate error because blood sticks are sometimes difficult and of course more unnecessary blood draws are not a good practice for time and for the patient. 

moving on, dr. ronnie sims came in within a half hour of our arrival and assured us that the chest x-ray was just fine and after asking some good questions he just wanted to draw another set of enzymes to make sure that there were no cardiac issue. 

the blood draw was taken quickly however the turnaround was an hour, which could have been done in fifteen minutes, but once they got the results we were expeditiously discharged out and we're on our way. 

there's no way for me to know if our experience was typical for this er, since we have nothing to compare it to, but overall they staff did a very nice job. 

bottom line: #1 son is well and this hospital er does a very nice job!

the worst clinic ever. i came today and spent here more than one hour waiting in a line. at the moment of signing in i told to receptionist ashley that i will step out and be waiting outside to be outside of crowd at the time of pandemic. ashley acknowledged it. then she failed to tell it to the nurse when the nurse called me. after that, ashley yelled at me and placed me in the end of the line making me waiting for another hour.

i was here overnight after surgery. i was told my daughter could be there during my pre op until they took me to surgery. they did not allow her back and actually had my family go home. the doctor came out to talk to my family and was not told they were not allowed to stay. everything went well until i was taken to my room. i was ignored. the iv machine beeped for 20 minutes. i could not get anyone to come help. i finally pushed every button till it was turned off. i was told i needed to walk to go home that day. no one came to help me.  i begged the nurses to help me get up to walk but no one came. i had to spend the night when i could have gone home. the nurses only came if i needed meds or to take my vitals. another patient screamed all evening and i was told by my nurses they were looking after her. i was ignored because she was screaming. if my family could have been there i could have gotten something to drink or gone to the bathroom. if you will not let families stay because of covid-19 then nurses need to pay attention to their patients. i owe more money because i had to stay the night when i wanted to go home.

this is where my sister - despite all odds - did not die from covid19 complications.  this is where she received excellent care from people trying to heal others while learning about the disease as they went along. a nurse called us three times a day to give us updates on her progress and well-being while she was on the ventilator and in a medically-induced coma.

they didn't just take care of my sister at this hospital, they took care of us as well with calls from the people caring for her and the chaplain's office.  everything sucks right now but for those of us who had it worse for month i can tell you that it isn't their job to check in on the family it was appreciated. these people are tired, they're working hard, and too many of y'all are rude, ungrateful, and going out of your way to make their job harder.  they could have been jaded or looked to self-care first but they didn't. i appreciate it and so does my whole family.  

not being able to see my sister would have been so much harder in the dark.  

***my sister gave the appropriate hipa release for them to do all this.

i had the fortunate opportunity to be a patient here at the end of february, 2020. yes, right before all elective surgeries were cancelled due to the corona virus, or covid-19. the staff was absolutely wonderful! check in was easy, as you go up to the 2nd floor, and the check in desk is right there by the elevators, you can't miss it. the waiting room is comfortable, with nice seating, and plenty of it. there are tables there for your use as well. free coffee and tea too.

they have a nice system in place, where there are rooms that you are taken to, once surgery/procedure is done, and your family/friends talk to the doctor/surgeon about how things went. this is done in private. there is also a board where your family/friends can watch the progress of your surgery/procedure as well, all by the number assigned to you when you check in.

the hospital is big, very big. it's clean too. there is a nice cafeteria, and a daz boggs as well. there is a gift shop on the first floor, and a baby joe's gift shop, if i remember correctly, on the 4th floor as well.

parking is easy too. there are several garages with free parking. or, use the valet service, which is right there by the front door. 

the staff is wonderful, as well as all volunteers, and basically, everyone. 

my stay at the hospital was a good one. i was always in good hands. i never needed anything either. the room was comfortable, and i had it to myself, i didn't have to share it with anyone. the food was good too.

if i ever have to have surgery again, i wouldn't hesitate when told that the surgery would be at st. joseph hospital. thanks for the excellent care!

this is specifically about the er. i went in for having covid symptoms that were irritating my asthma. they basically took me back to a room and scolded me for being there. the doc even admitted how shaky the test is. they didn't listen to my breathing or anything. i went home and had an asthma attack but was too scared to go back and face rejection and humiliation again. eventually went back and was hospitalized for covid. hospitalization was better than er but the er needs to rethink their priorities. this is a pandemic with a deadly virus and inaccurate test, treat all your patients with respect and listen to their symptoms, not their false negative. future hospitalization could have been avoided if you cared the first time.

took my son to the er for a fever 102 and to request a covid test. er dr and nurse were wonderful. so kind and helpful. 4 stars for the experience. however they informed me i should get tested asap and provided me the out paiteint lab to go 1st thing the next morning to get tested.

this review is 1 star for the out patient lab. terrible experience. it is so disturbing to me that a hospital can be run so poorly! we arrived 10min after 7am, they hadn't opened yet. we gave our information to the person at check in, she quoted us an hour wait and said someone would call when ready. (pouring rain outside and they don't let you sit inside) after 75 minutes we finally get a phone call informing us that they do not test adults and we would not be seen. i have now waited close to 2 hours in the rain. spoke to a supervisor (who was very nice) but could do nothing. they sent us away. 

1. train your staff. it is pathetic to think a hospital/lab can be run so poorly.

2. educate your staff on who can get tested and where. 

my reccomedations... no idea! i am extremely disappointed and now heading home to a sick child with no peace of mind!

this hospital is so disconnected. the fact that this is a major children's hospital and still standing is astounding.

this review pertains to the care my 36 year old son received at porter adventist hospital after being transferred from mercy regional medical center (durango) almost two years ago.  two years is the length of time that i have spent trying to get justice for brian.  the lies, the condescending sympathy and the refusal to release recorded medical records (until i hired an attorney) have added greatly to the pain of losing my son.  brian had gone to the ed at mercy where he had a ct and egd the next day.   a giant pseudoaneurysm measuring 10.2 cm was found along with gastric and esophageal varices caused by thrombosis and erosive esophagitis most likely caused by multiple episodes of vomiting blood.  the mercy gi doctor shared the findings with a mercy vascular surgeon.  both doctors said they did not have the skill sets to treat brian and recommended that he be transferred to another hospital.  the vascular surgeon had to have known that brian needed urgent surgery because of the high probability of the giant pseudoaneurysm rupturing.  (brian had never been told that he had a giant pseudoaneurysm. he was told he had a blood clot.) to arrange the transfer, a mercy hospitalist had two conversations with a porter hospitalist and one conversation with a porter hepatologist.  the porter hospitalist also talked to a centura connect representative saying he didn't think porter doctors had skills beyond the skills that the mercy doctors had.  the transfer was still approved. the mercy hospitalist read the impressions from the egd that did not mention the size of the pseudoaneurysm.  the size of the pseudoaneurysm was only mentioned in the findings.  neither the porter hepatologist nor the porter hospitalist bothered to pull brian's records during or after the phone conversations.  they just listened to the mercy hospitalist read the impressions for 5 minutes.  the conversations started out talking about the need for surgery and then change to gi being the main reason for the transfer.  the pseudoaneurysm became a secondary concern.  brian left mercy on a flight for life plane in fair condition, but he actually had dangerously high blood pressure, a map reading with alert next to it and 9 out of 10 pain.  he was given an opioid for the pain right before the plane took off.  there was no plan for surgery when brian arrived at porter, instead he was assigned to an inpatient room.  shortly after arriving, brian's medical chart showed bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 4:39am bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 7:30am mottling skin, blue/pale - nothing was done. at 8:00am bp/high/alert!, map/alert! - nothing was done.  at 9:15am - brian was found moaning, doctor performed cpr for 45 minutes.  brian was pronounced dead at 10:03am.  the nurse manager called to say brian died and within the same minute says, what do you want us to do with his body?  my son's autopsy shows that he died from the rupture of a known aneurysm.  brian actually died from the lack of treatment, and an inept medical system.  per john hopkins hospital study - medical errors account for 1/3 of hospital deaths, but you will never see medical error as the cause of death on an autopsy report or on a death certificate.  as of today, there is a reported 60,726 covid-19 deaths in the us.  as of today, the number of deaths in 2020 caused by medical errors is probably much higher than the covid-19 deaths. medical errors are a silent, rampant epidemic and they are hidden from the patients' families.
