i can't even begin to express my gratitude to the staff in the emergency department, and all of the other nurses, doctors, and technicians who treated me with extraordinary patience and kindness during my stay at mercy general. 

i went to the emergency department in serious condition (both physically and mentally,) and due to the covid-19 crisis, i was skeptical that the hospital would have the energy, means, interest, or (wo)man-power to address my medical and psychiatric needs. that skepticism soon vanished after experiencing the care and thoughtfulness of each and every nurse and doctor who treated me during my 4-night stay.

what's more is that my insurance partially lapsed and would only cover one night of care. the hospital ate the bill for the remaining nights, which saved me much heartache and financial strain down the road. it was an unmerited act of mercy. this hospital lives up to it's name!

in addition, i had no family that was able to pick me up due to the shelter in place ordinance, so i was concerned about traveling back home to santa cruz on amtrak fresh out of the hospital from a severe illness. once again, mercy stepped in to save the day- they arranged a ride all the way home to santa cruz.

i have been hospitalized on two other occasions in my adult life, and this experience far exceeded all of my other visits, and the attention to detail and empathy of the staff here far surpassed my expectations. i am so grateful for all of the providers who helped save my life. thank you all!!!

far away from this place as much as possible.  i had to go to the er and experienced malpractice from a doctor with pathetic medical skills and even worse people skills.  i was there for 5 1/2 hours, in an empty er, the first 4 1/2 alone in the room with no follow up contact by the doctor and no discussion about the tests he was ordering.  in fact, he just disappeared and i never saw him after a wound, they still charged me for unnecessary tests.  while the 2nd doctor was nice and ultimately redid the physical exam and gave me a correct diagnosis in about 2 minutes, he was mostly back peddling and trying to protect his incompetent coworker as i complained about the lack of professional medical care i was receiving.  i will never go back, despite it being such a convenient location i sat on this review update for about 6 months, as i wanted to make sure i was not reacting to my emotions connected to my medical issue.  but now that i've had time to think, i feel even stronger than i did before.  my condition was a simple diagnosis, and they largely failed.  imagine if it had been more complicated or life threatening?  they will get no more attempts at wasting my time, money, or my health, as i will be going elsewhere.

this review is for the er and hospital.

what i thought was a routine visit to my cardiologist suddenly turned south when, after some testing, he announced i had to get to the er immediately. that's how i found myself here in the emergency room being told i needed triple bypass heart surgery. 

spoiler alert: i'm still alive

the surgeon (dr. hargrove) was confident and calming. she proved to be exceptionally skilled and performed a successful surgery despite some minor complications along the way. i can't speak highly enough about her.

during several days of recovery, my nurses - there were many - and their support staff were competent, caring and all-around fantastic. actually there was one exception but i believe it was due to inexperience. i was impressed with all the controls they had in place to protect patients while this 2020 pandemic is going on.

as expected, the food was generally lousy although breakfasts were okay. the beds were not the most comfortable. and if you want a good night's sleep a hospital is not the place to be, between getting poked for blood tests all night and patients in other rooms making every type of noise imaginable echo down the hallways. most recovery rooms are double occupancy but i was lucky to have a private room so my stay was probably better than most. 

follow up by cardiac rehab and my surgeon was excellent. 

i certainly hope you won't ever need to come here but if you do, rest assured they will take good care of you. a 4.5 rating from me.

review: came for an x-ray. the tech was good, though don't appreciate the personal question at the registrations, which had nothing to do with my visit for the day. also, and very strangely enough, the woman at the registration wanted me to initial my agreement using her pen, strangely, with my bare hands -- which she claimed she sanitized. i cannot imagine how many people before me have used that very pen with their bare hands.  additionally, when a nurse came to measure my temperature, for pandemic reasons, she did so  standing perpendicular to me, so that i'm less of a threat to her, nonetheless she was facing me, thereby a small threat to me.   the woman at the registration could have offered to ask me to satirize my hands and give me gloves for my protection;  but who cares about me anyway, it's all about their safety!

i am only giving a 2 stars bc some of the clinical staff are nice. first of issue was back when the pandemic had just started, i scheduled a telephonic appt with a provider to discuss s/s. only to be given a questionnaire to fill out and the provider sending me a message through my portal that basically stated that i was fine and if i get any worse call the hospital. that interaction cost me $35! never spoke to anyone! what a joke. then today i call the lab to see if my testing had been analyzed since it's almost been a week and my doctor claims she doesn't see anything and i get a lab tech with a smart alec attitude that was very condescending. in the end he did not provide any info, i did not ask for test results as i work in the medical field and know that these can not be given by anyone other than your doctor all i wanted is to make sure my testing was submitted so if there was an error i could go get retested. bottom line there is no excuse to be treated so rudely when you are a patient nervously awaiting results. he could of just nicely said please call your doctor we can not give any info but he proceeded to be extremely rude and sarcastic. so disappointed in their customer service.

i had the unfortunate experience of having to visit the er for my teenage son last night.   i was headed straight for dell children's, as all parents of children should, but he was complaining of horrible dizziness and he had a head injury, so i did not feel comfortable driving that far with him.  in hindsight, i wish we had gone to dell.  

screened at front door for covid and masked.  no problem here other than we were not given any introductions.   from screening, through initial triage, i don't have any serious complaints.   my son was identified as a "trauma alert" in triage, due to the mechanism of his injury, and we were quickly wheeled back. i am uncertain of anyone's role up to this point as all staff who came into contact with us failed to tell us their name or role (with the exception of being told we were  "in" triage, no name or role to the person who completed that task.)

once in the room, my son was taken for ct within 5 minutes.  he had been wheeled to the room, placed on a monitor and left lying in a cold, wet swimsuit. upon return from ct, the pa came by to see him.  she was attentive and concerned.  she gave him a thorough exam, but had trouble finding any nursing staff who could assist her to roll him properly to clear c-spine.  throughout the duration of our stay, the nurses were much less than attentive.  there is an informative board on the wall that tells you the date.  ours read yesterday's date and it is unlikely the male nurse attending to us was named paige or esther, as identified by the board.   

the nursing staff was very disappointing.  they were standing at the nursing station conversing about the 6 year delinquency of required trainings for one of the nurse's at work that evening.  never offered a call bell, had to search for a nurse every time, the bathroom floor was covered in urine, my son was never removed from his wet clothes, taken off the wet fitted sheet (despite multiple bed transfers), never offered a warm blanket (standard of care for trauma alert). they did not operate as a team.  if i asked for something, the other nurses relayed the request to our assigned nurse rather than offering to help. when my son left for mri, evs actually assisted mri staff with the bed transfer because the nurses were sitting at the nurses station and did not offer to help.  

the pa was attentive.  if it were not for her, this review would be 1 star.  the pa
took pictures and relayed them to her attending physician, who was apparently involved in care but never came by to see him.  my son was never asked to rate his pain.  no follow up for the tylenol i requested he be given.  the nurses never asked him about his symptoms.   they did not ever assess him.  the only true assessment was completed by the pa and one by a triage nurse.  discharge instructions by the nurse included reading me the titles off the papers and i was told to fill the cephalexin, "which is an antibiotic, i think", the nurse said.  yes- it is.  nurses make all of the difference.   unfortunately, the nurses this evening showed the difference it makes when they don't take pride in their work.

i checked into sutter er on march 9th, 2020, because i thought i could be miscarrying my pregnancy and urgent care suggested i go to the er to get an ultrasound. i walked in, the lobby was empty (due to the covid19 scare), sanitized my own seat, and everything went smoothly after checking in. i had no pain, i was offered wheel chairs, but i preferred to walk, the er was also empty, and i even saw nurses sitting and texting on their phones.  i had my blood drawn for standard blood testing and two ultrasounds that showed a baby's heartbeat (i skipped out on the urine test due to lack of cups in the ultrasound room).  on the way out, i asked how much the visit was going to cost me, "$250- do you want to pay now or would you like us to bill you?"- i asked them to send me the bill. i thought this was a pretty successful precautionary visit- until i got the bill.

they are trying to charge me for a level 4 (levels start at 1 and go up to 5- 5 is the most serious and most expensive) service charge. that alone is over $3,000- the charges add up to almost $6,000 not including my insurance coverage. now, i know i walked into an emergency room, and that it would cost more than my less-than-a-hundred-dollars copay, but really?? everything that was done that day could have been done by my doctor and the lab for under $100. i decided i wouldn't dispute the charges for the lab work, doctor's fee, and ultrasounds- but the level 4 charge needed to be reduced. the price is absolutely unjust and unreasonable for the standard service i received.

i called sutter, who directed me to my insurance company, called them and realized the issue was not my insurance...   i called sutter again, was given a number for something i didn't need- i can't tell you how many times i have called or how many people i have talked to, but i would say i talked to at least 5 of the regular billing department agents, and then i asked to escalate it, that was another person, and then i was told to take it up with the er doctor directly, called the er department who gave me to the department manager who needed to talk to the next person...  this has been going on since march. i have played endless phone tag, left messages, and i've gotten the run-around. it is now almost the end of may and i still haven't talked to anyone who can do anything about anything, and i'm damn tired of people trying to explain things to me, when they can't give me answers to questions i have been asking. it is almost time for my bill to get shoveled over to collections because they refuse to help me. 

i can say whole-heartedly that i feel i have been scammed by sutter. i am in the middle of my pregnancy and have canceled all my appointments. i delivered my first baby with sutter, but not this one, not after this wretched experience. how could i ever trust them again?

switching to kaiser permanente is definitely on the table right now.

(it is; i confirmed with my medical team and i was told that i am at high risk and must take extra precautions at all times, on top of the pandemic.) she was constantly bugging me about moving me out of my single room - which was the only way i was discharged from the full service hospital facility to kindred: it must be a private room.

review:
by now, many of my fellow yelpers have heard about my recent battle with brain cancer.  i had no idea that i had a fist sized tumor in my right temple until i had a massive seizure that caused me to throw myself to the flow, striking my side table next to my bed so hard with my jaw that i broke the legs off!  i don't remember any of that but remember waking in the hospital with a breathing tube in my mouth and feeling somewhat confused.

within a few days my surgery was scheduled and they successfully removed a small high grade tumor as well as the massive low grade tumor.  i spent nearly a week in the hospital and must say that everyone i came into contact with was friendly and caring and encouraging, so i felt the care i received throughout my stay (and my recent follow up visits) has been excellent.

even the food from the cafeteria was pretty good.  not high cuisine, but palatable and with enough diversity that i felt like i had decent choices for each meal.  in fact, my only complaint is that they could boost their wifi since over the course of the week, there wasn't much i could do other than take naps.  streaming on my phone was not very successful.  but honestly, i probably needed the naps to recover from the huge surgery (42 staples needed) more than i needed to watch some episode of a tv show.

i feel like the staff was so upbeat and supportive including helping my wife and i find our way around the hospital.  if anything, they may have given too much information upfront since i am not well versed in medical and medicinal terminology.  fortunately, my wife takes great notes and was able to coordinate all my follow-up appointments for me and to fill my pill box so that i took the right pills at the right frequency.

when i met with the surgeon and oncologist, i felt they explained things in terms i could understand and they prepared me for the upcoming challenge of the multi cycle treatment plan which starts next week.  i understand what each phase is supposed to provide and with so many ways of attacking my disease, i am confident that i will one day be back to my independent self.  it won't be easy, but i felt each doctor and nurse i dealt with cared about me and did their best to make sure i knew they were in this fight with me.

on my follow up visit where i was fitted with a radiation mask, i met a completely different set of staff and each of them was equally helpful whether it was on getting registered, or someone escorting us to the right department for our appointments.  just wonderful people who are doing their best to help the patients in their care.  what more can a patient ask for?  i am thankful for the good folks at methodist who literally saved my life.  and despite having an initial prognosis of only having 15 months if i don't continue with treatments, their support and plan gives me hope that i will one day be back to writing more reviews as i explore our state, one county at a time.

methodist is a great place and benefits with its connection to the greater iu health organization including the goodman hall neuroscience center across the street.

thank you to all the staff who took care of me.

review: i've been home about two hours now. i've debated for two hours whether i wanted to say anything or not. i've been sick since monday; it's saturday. it started out a little cough here and there. it progressively got a little worse. i started running low grade fevers and then would get chills. my nose was super stuffy. i thought ok i'm coming down with a sinus infection. i got antibiotics. they didn't work. as a matter of fact i started feeling worse; run down, fatigued, my body has been aching. today i started feeling short of breath. my chest hurt but not in that way you would think would come with a prolonged cough. more like a heavy, achy feeling. i've struggled to regain my breath several times today but i still didn't feel emergent. i weighed the options of getting health care with covid 19 so rampant but because i started struggling with air today and after asking the opinions of my triage professionals ( yes i work in healthcare) i decided i'd go to the er after i finished my shift. once i got to the room the dr explained he was ordering a flu test, a strep test (even though i had no sore throat at all) and a chest x-ray. results came back negative for everything and chest x ray showed no pneumonia. the dr tells me they won't test me for the corona virus unless i am admitted to the hospital and the only way for that to happen is if i had more emergent breathing issues. even though i was struggling to catch breaths my o2 sat was 99%. he tells me though that with all my symptoms he cannot rule out the virus and i was to return home to self quarantine until april 13. today is the 4th. upon discharge a different nurse that i hadn't met came in to give me my papers. i asked her, "how do i know if i need to come back?" this is why i'm writing. her answer floored me. she told me i shouldn't come back unless "i'm so out of breath (i) can't talk or if i'm turning blue." i asked if she was serious. she tells me "yes but if you're turning blue call 911 so they can get you oxygen on the way here." y'all i've been in healthcare for 15 years. i also have chronic health issues that have had me in and out of drs and ers and never in my life have i heard something so outrageous or felt treated so insignificant. i know there's a pandemic. i'm essential so i go to work and come home. i don't go out unless i absolutely have to. i heavily weighed wether i should go in or not and the care i received was what it should have been. they weren't full of patients, in fact it was pretty empty for 20:45 on a saturday. i know they are tired and over worked but something more needs to be done because if this is how we are screening patients for this virus that truly have all the symptoms no wonder people keep getting sick.
